212619.overview: A horizontally scrolling space shooter created by Inutilis and released in 2003. Created with AMOS. Source code included.

212620.overview:
Spelltris from Gerry Quinn on the Amiga. Spelltris is similar to Tetris, except that single letters fall down and you have to make (English) words from them.  If you make a word it disappears and the letters above fall down - sometimes causing more words to be formed.  (It's more like Columns really...) 

The game recognises 25000 words.  There are options to make the game harder or easier, depending on your skill level.  It can speak the words or play music.

Spelltris was on the coverdisk of Amiga User International (September 1995).

212621.overview: Create your colony outpost, setup your power and manufacturing. Trade for what you need and set up spies and armies in this game which is very reminiscent of Civilization. This homebrew game was created by Christian Kargl and released in 2000. There was both an unregistered demo version and the full registered version of this game.

212622.overview: Practice and compete in swimming, shooting, gymnastics and archery competitions. This game is related to Sports Challenge (Summer) which offers a different set of events. If you can qualify n the events your score will be recorded.

212623.overview: A public domain space invaders style shooter from  4 Seasons Soft, released in 1991.

212624.overview: Made with AMOS and Personal Paint, this shooter from Garfield Benjamin tasks you with stopping the alien ships from hitting your base. Shoot the ships, bomb the incoming energy attacks, shoot those in the air. When the blue line is depleted, you will move to the next sector.

212625.overview: Practice and compete in diving, shooting, sprinting and cycling competitions. This game is related to Sports Challenge (Spring) which offers a different set of events. If you can qualify n the events your score will be recorded.

212626.overview: An expanded and more colorful version of Battlezone, with more vehicle types. HUD in top left shows location of enemies on the screen. Alerts help you know when the enemy is firing at you. Blast the enemy tanks and vehicles and get the high score. This version is public domain and was released by Maciek Sawicki in 1994.

212627.overview: A fun, Italian language Tetris game, not that language enters much into it, created by Gargoyle Software with distribution and intro titles from Ram Jam.

212628.overview: An updated version of Super Caztri including English language support instead of just Italian and AGA compatibility.

212629.overview: A split screen 2 player shooter written by Brian Hambley of Hambo Software. Additional mission data disks were to be available from the author. Super Combat 3 is a head to head battle for 2 players, set over 3 levels. Points are scored for shooting the enemy and rescuing hostages, or by destroying your opponents base. Weapons and power ups can be found and used by each player, you can carry 2 weapons at a time, each with limited ammo.

212630.overview:
Top view racing game for up to 4 players, super Sprint style, coded in Amos by Sylvain Zangiacomi. – Championship: it's a performance race, you have to come first and be the fastest on the lap to collect as many points as possible.

– Wild: it's a merciless war, each destroyed car earns you a point, the winner of a race also receives a point.

– Scenario: allows you to select certain scenarios (countryside, desert, city, hell) to discover them, points are earned according to the order of arrival only.

For each mode, you can choose the number of races, the number of laps per race, the level of the CPU cars, and for the Scenario mode, the types of circuits chosen.

212631.overview:
Basically, Super It is a computerized version of It, or Tig, as we used to call it in these parts. Four players can compete, and the person who is It can Tig any of the others at any time, whereupon they become It. The game is played against the clock, and the person who is It when the time runs out is the loser. 

The three Amigos obviously never played by Cheshire rules. Whereas when I was at school it was a well known law that "You can't Tiggy butcher" - a person who was It couldn't Tig back the person who Tigged them - it's perfectly acceptable to do so in Super It. Still, it seems that the rest of the 
world plays a different set of pub pool. 
 
Game came with an included Super iT map editor.

212632.overview:
Super Robin is a new Amiga game created by AmigaPD using the Reality Game Creator Software. The game has a total of 31 short levels made up of different zones.

The object of the game is quite simple, collect all the fruit and then head to the exit to the far right of the level. Some fruit is also contained in blocks which have to be hit from below using your characters head. Enemies can be avoided by jumping over them or running away.

There are teleporter doors – to access these push up on your joystick and press fire when in front of the door. There are also switches – to activate these push up on your joystick and then press fire. When you get to the end of the level you sometimes have the option for two exits – the bottom door option will take you to a bonus level. Erik Hogan created the menu select screen for CD32 version. Simone Bernacchia has provided the in game music for the full game version – the other music provided for the different zones under the practice option have been taken from the Assassins Public Domain disk.

The Dylan Demo option on the menu takes you to a demo of ‘Dizzy Adventure Clone’, also created using the Reality Adventure skeleton disk.

212734.overview: An aerial dogfighting game built to support even the A4000 Amigas and released to public domain by Chris Hodges in 1995.

212737.overview: An update to the earlier Strikes -N- Spares, a bowling game for up to 8 players. A unique control system uses the mouse to control the overall direction and speed of the throw. It has all the features a bowling game should have but doesn't take forever to set up.

212738.overview:
A side-scrolling shoot-em-up. Kill the aliens and rescue the little spacemen! Created by J. Kennedy and D. Irvine. Warning: this is not a drill! Alien fleet approaching Terran system. Central control predicts the alien fleet will attack the following locations: Terran Lunar System, Planet Earth, Mars. Mission objectives: Protect humanoids from abduction and mutation. 

Available weapons: Multiple fire laser, limited smart bombs and hyperspace entry shield.

212739.overview: A strategy submariner wargame originally released in the U.S. in 1993, SUBVERSION was released to the wider Amiga market in 1995 on budget by Guidlhall and coded by Daryl Schroeder.

212740.overview: A nice, quiet strategy space game for up to 4 players by John Smit, released in 1992.

212741.overview:
In Stable Masters II the player again takes the role of a horse trainer to raise and train a thoroughbred horse in preparation of horse derby races. The player must first purchase a horse (each of which performs differently in racing). Then the player must choose a jockey that can ride and work with the horse. Finally the player must pick a race course. The player's choices affect the outcome of the race. If the player's horse wins, then the player earns money needed to fund the hiring fees and stable expenses.

This game is the sequel to Stable Masters and the prequel to Stable Masters III.

212742.overview: In this updated and improved version of the Stable Masters franchise you again take on the role of a horse trainer to raise and train a thoroughbred horse in preparation of horse derby races. The player must first purchase a horse (each of which performs differently in racing). Then the player must choose a jockey that can ride and work with the horse. Finally the player must pick a race course. The player's choices affect the outcome of the race. If the player's horse wins, then the player earns money needed to fund the hiring fees and stable expenses. This game has improved graphics, but only supports a single player mode.

212774.overview: Super Pac-Man '92 is an action game that got released by Pendle Europa for the Commodore Amiga in 1992 only in Denmark; as its name suggests, it stars Namco's signature character Pac-Man, and in the spirit of his early official games, the player has to direct him around a two-dimensional maze while avoiding ghosts (but rather than a number of individual ghosts, there are three different types of them: Wanderers, who are green like Funky and easy to avoid, Romers, who are red like Blinky and might chase Pac-Man, and Chasers, who are gray like Spunky and will chase Pac-Man). There is only one type of bonus item that will appear beneath the ghost regenerator, a trio of berries (one blue, one red and one yellow) which is worth a mystery bonus when eaten - and even though Pac-Man will receive an extra life every 10000 points, the game creates the illusion of not having a scoring system, for the player's score is only seen at the start of a round and after finishing one. The mazes, which advance after every even-numbered round, are also too large for the Amiga's monitor, so will scroll according to Pac-Man's location, and when Pac-Man eats a ghost after consuming a power pellet (or "acid pill" as the game calls them) to turn them vulnerable, the ghost will still be edible when his eyes return to the regenerator until the power pellet's effect has worn off, except if the pellet's effect wears off first.

212776.overview:
A humorous ice hockey game Stix N Trax is a cool new 2 player simultaneous ice hockey game. You have to  get the puck and score against the other player, first player to reach 10  wins!

 It was coded in Blitz Basic v2.1 using Dpaint5 to create the graphics. Sounds  were grabbed for the crowd using Megalosound v1.37. The crowd sounds were  meant to add humour to the game and make it more realistic, the graphics may  not be very impressive because I did them myself ;). One final point is that  it may need an accelerated Amiga because of the constant blitting of the  crowd. I'm not sure though because it has only been tested on my 040/25.
 
 Welcome to Stix N Trax! A game made specifically for entry into the Amiga  Format readers game section! The game is essentially a one on one 2 player simultaneous Hockey game, there are two NHL hockey teams to choose from. Each  team consists of one pro player. The players must control their Hockey Player  using the joypad and try and score in the opposing players goal. Pushing  the fire button whilst in possession of the puck will fire it in the  direction which you are traveling. The puck's speed and direction is  proportional to the players speed and direction. Pushing and holding the  fire button whilst not in possession of the puck lets you gain control  of your goalkeeper. The goalkeepers job is to stop the puck going in the  net by moving in the way of it. When the puck hits the keeper it will be  catapulted outwards back into play. The winner of the game will be the player who gets 10 goals first.

212777.overview: A 3D styled shoot em up, that according to Galahad on the EAB forums, is an early pre-release for what became Guardian AGA, the Starfox/Starwing like game on the SNES. Basically this game was never intended to be released! Also thanks of course goes to Earok, and the original developers Acid Software!" Get your mission objectives, take out the sentries protecting the objective target, but you'll need to take out the power sources for them or they will blast you out of the skies. Keep your eyes on those skies as enemy ships will appear and try to take you out. Keep your shield power high!

212785.overview:
A German language PICROSS clone created by Sebastian Beloch aka Sebel. It is a a nonogramme puzzle game. 
The player is presented with a grid, surrounded by numbers on the top and left sides. These numbers represent the number of squares on that row or column that shall be filled. On a 5x5 grid, a number five means that the entire row or column should form a straight line across the grid, whereas the numbers ”2, 1” on the left mean that that row should have one line of 2 filled squares and another shorter line of 1 square. These lines must have at least one blank square to separate them. Using deduction, it is possible to fill in all the right squares when viewed holistically.

213431.overview: Space Pong is a one or two player Pong Clone with three levels of difficulty, from Mauro Antonio Radice created for the Amiga to Celebrate 50th Anniversary of Atari Pong.

213662.overview:
Get 100% every week on your spelling test at school!
Speller Bee utilizes First Byte's Smooth Talker speech technology to give you a powerful talking spelling tool. Although there are grade level lists stored on the disk, for the first time you can enter your own spelling words. Speller Bee assists you until you have successfully spelled each word correctly and then gives you a practice 'Spelling Bee' to test your skill. In addition, you can use your spelling lists to play 3 exciting games that hide, scramble and change your words until you spell them correctly and win!

213892.overview: The sequel to the popular Formula1 racing game played in a third person perspective in the mold of Pole Position. the game consists of tracks based on real world locations and this disk has more of those to experience. These can be played in a competition consisting of three laps or in a practice mode with 99 laps (or until the player presses the escape key). In each race there are 23 AI controlled cars to compete against. The game is playable in three difficulties: novice, amateur and professional. The car has six gears that have to be changed manually and a boost feature can also be used for faster acceleration.

214093.overview:
Spider is a game of patience which uses two regular decks of playing cards. The tableau consists of ten columns of cards, initially with 44 cards face down with a row of 10 cards face up on top. Spider Game Screen

The object of the game is to manipulate the cards to assemble complete suits with the king at the base of the pile and the ace at the top. When a complete suit is assembled it can be removed from play. The game is won if all eight suits are removed.

Cards are moved from the top of columns, either individually, or in groups. The cards are then placed on other columns in decending order, regardless of suit.

The top card of any column is available to move, while groups of cards can only be moved if they are a descending run of the same suit.
Features
Spider is fully configurable with all of the following items changable within the program:

    Screen Mode and Size
    Screen Font
    Card Set
    Card Back

Card Sets may be edit using any paint program and converted using the make_cards program which is available seperately. The format for editing Card Sets, which is described with the make_cards program allows you to change the size, image and even the shape of the cards. You can also define up to twelve different card backs for the set.

Spider allows games to be saved and when reloaded you can:

    Play the game again from the start.
    Continue the game from where you left off.
    Watch a replay of the game as played previously.

214150.overview: Solar Lords by Alistair Duncan of Tiger Software, released as Shareware in 1993. You and up to 3 of your friends control warlords maneuvering to control six planets. Try to increase your per turn income to outpace your rivals, increase your military power keep up your science rating. Use spies, buy capitol ships, armor and outfit your fleet and rule the galaxy.

214285.overview: A public domain rendition of the Monopoly board game by Mathew Wilson, released initially in 1994, with later updates. It has lots of configurable game options so you can play the way to often do at home.

214310.overview: Shooting Star is a shoot 'em up played from a top down perspective with movement in multiple directions. The objective of each level is to collect ten yellow rings which happens automatically when moving the space ship over them. Once they have all been collected the player has to move to the exit which will transport the ship to the next level. There are plenty of hostile space ships which attempt to stop the player and these have to be avoided or killed. There are also plenty of other obstacles such as walls that the player has to avoid crashing into and often these are moving or changing form. The player has six lives and when they are all gone it is game over.

214322.overview: Soccer Supremo is a football management game, developed by Pirate and published by Crysys Software, which was released in Europe in 1987.

214325.overview: Space Baller is an action game, developed and published by International Software Köln, which was released in Europe in 1987. And later released in both the International Arcade Action and the Amiga Stars Collection compilation packs. There were two versions, one with a blue ball and the other with a red and white Amiga ball. Humour, electric atmosphere and superb game play. Use the joystick to guide the bouncing ball through space, pick up different objects and bonuses but watch out for the aliens trying to shoot you down.

214345.overview: A fast moving racing car game, requiring skill and lightning reflexes. In order to beat your opponent you must surround him with the energy beam your car leaves behind it - but be warned it destroys everything it touches. 1 or 2 player option.

214351.overview: Strange New World is a horizontally scrolling Shooter, developed and published by Softgang, which was released in Europe in 1987.

214353.overview:
Have you ever wanted to try your hand at being a surgeon? The skill, the pressure, the split-second life or death decisions, this program has it all.
Operate in real time and deal with the complications of the surgery. Keep an eye on the EKG monitor and the patient's blood pressure while you exercise your skill.
Feel the satisfaction of a successful operation!!
The Surgeon is also educational!! While performing the surgery you will learn the parts of a human body, medical terminologies and the steps involved in a surgical operation.

214478.overview: Your objective in this game is to bring the barrels back to the black fields. Game also known as Slider and had slightly different game screen.

214551.overview: SameGame is an addictive puzzle game, which is played on a rectangular field, filled with coloured balls. The object of the game is to clear the field by removing groups of pieces of the same colour. You get points for each group you remove and the larger the group, the more points you get. To get the highest score you need to make large blocks of one colour.

214572.overview: This is a football management game similar to other productions and created in 1998 in AMOS Professional. In it, you guide small Santa Monica FC from fourth league to the very top. Twelve leagues to choose from. Polish, English and German versions included. Choose your line up and position. You need 3 points for win, play each team twice. The best three teams will be promoted, the bottom 3 will be relegated. Domestic cup is played in one leg rounds. In case of a tie, the game will go into extra time until the first scored goal. All European cups are played in a cup system with two leg rounds with same rules for a tie. Substitutions can be made after 7 minutes of game time. Manage finances, sign new sponsorship deals!

214574.overview:
Published in 1993 by L.K. Avalon, Saper was an above-average platform puzzle elements title in its time. Saper is a two-dimensional platform game with elements of puzzle-solving created by Marek Pasek, Danuta Sienkowska and Henryk Cygert for L.K. Avalon Poland. The story tells of a criminal organization, which managed to steal important NATO documents. CIA agents have failed to recover the documents, therefore the authorities decide to blow up the headquarters of criminals. The building has many explosives installed. The player has to destroy all the bombs which are visible on the screen and then reach an exit point. Some of the bombs and exits are not easily reachable. To get access to them it is necessary to move some tiles too. The basis for the completion of the mission is the order of detonation explosive devices. There are tiles which have unique purposes. An additional difficulty is the time limit, to pass each of the 64 levels of the game authors dedicate 120 seconds. The player will face as well disappearing tiles, exploding mines or surfaces of ice that move the player to the first no ice area. In contrast, the expanding plant, the detonator of all bombs or the teleport should greatly facilitate the task.

The game has a built-in editor which allows to modify all the completed boards.

214575.overview: A German language chess\schach board game released to Germany and Austria by Schatztruhe in 1994. It was coded by Oliver Seidel and Philipp Braun.

214576.overview: A nicely done version of the Scrabble word board game by Vision and released in 1991. It included the ability to load a standard words (dictionary) file or to load a modified\new one of your creation. Word files from the Oxford English and Webster's dictionaries were created and available on the web.

214578.overview: A patience card game by DawnBringer. This is a fully playable solitaire game written by Richard DawnBringer Fhager in AMOS inspired by the Silicon Graphics version. Multiple cards can be moved at the same time. Auto move. HiRes graphics and a card locator built-in. Planned updates like an undo and statistics were never implemented. Cards of the same suit can be stacked in descending order, cards can be temporarily placed in the four slots.

214579.overview: A playable game demo a bit like an updated missile command, released by Howard Dortch in 1992. Deploy your equipment: AWACS, RADAR and Scudbuster anti missile systems prior to the game and then defend them from incoming missiles from above. If your command post is taken out, you lose the game.

214580.overview: A single player, puzzle shareshareware game created by Chris N. Benton and released in 1992, in it, you are in control of a white and blue blob, which has to cross a series of tiles to reach the exit. When you cross a yellow tile it is destroyed and all yellows MUST be destroyed to move on to the next level. You cannot pass over water (blue tiles), while a green square must be passed over twice. T squares are teleporters, grey tiles are stone and will not break or disappear. direction tiles only allow passage in the indicated directions. Get to the exit!

214582.overview: Senso is a puzzle\memory game, developed by Harald Muller and published by Intersoft, which was released in Europe in 1993. It is modeled after the electronic Simon Says game from Hasbro. In it, players must repeat random sequences of colors by pressing the colored pads in the correct order. It's fast-paced play, with flashing colors and sounds that can challenge you. Experience the fun as you repeat the patterns and advance to higher levels. Keep track of your score as you challenge friends or try to beat your own high score. It was part of several classic collections such as Gamers' Delight.

214583.overview: A solitaire card game from the fecund developer, Harald Müller (Mueller) and released in 1995.

214584.overview: Originally released in 1993 but having several updates and releases from Richard Brown of Tower Software until late 1994. This updated electronic version of Backgammon is a game for two players and originally sold for £10.00. It was released into PD Sep 2005. All rights to the game rest with Richard Brown of Tower Software. The disk image may be freely distributed as-is and only in its complete form. Updated Windows versions were also created that mirrored the final version of the game, version 1.11.

214585.overview: Shanghai II is a mahjong Solitaire\Shanghai board game from Alexis Katsadorakis and Kostas Pournaras that was first uploaded to Aminet on 1995-11-04 into directory 'game/board'. A second version with bug fixes was uploaded to Aminet on 1997-04-08 into directory 'game/think'.

214586.overview:
Shanghai '93 is a shareware Mahjongg game for the Amiga. Players can choose different sets of tiles to use and play the game in two modes: the 144 tile Dragon mode or the 100 tile Camel mode.

Like many other Mahjongg games, players move the mouse across the screen and click on two identical tiles to remove them from play. However only tiles that are exposed can be removed, making the strategy to know what order to remove them in. The game is won when all tiles are removed.

The player's screen always features a menu that allows the game to be restarted, a new game to be created, able to undo a move or finally forfeit the game and peek at the computer's suggested method of removing them.

Shanghai '93 Plus is the registered version of Shanghai '93 and adds extra tiles and extra levels.

214587.overview: Shanghai '98 is a German language level based mahjong clone. Try and clear the tiles as quickly as possible to progress to the next.  The game was featured on the German Amiga Special magazine (Amiga Special no. 6-7, June/July 1998 ) published by Media MbH in 1998.

214588.overview: A Japanese card game as "Hanafuda" was video game-ized. "Hanafuda" is the card game played in Japan from ancient times. The game was created in 2003 and updated as a 30th Amiga anniversary present in 2015 as Shokaku-68020 AMIGA 30th Anniversary Edition by Renya Iizuka of Pastel Spirits.

214589.overview: A single player casino game from Bryan Black. Shoot Pontoon is simply a more money oriented version of everyone's fave card game Pontoon, Blackjack or 21. You start off with one card each and must bet based on this card. The banker will now deal you another card. From here you can now stick (if you have more than 16), twist (which costs you nothing but the banker will know your card) or buy by adding to the pot to buy another card, but the bet remains the same. If you have 14 or less with 2 cards you can also burn to get 2 new cards. If you win against the banker you will take your bets back from the pot as well as the same amount from the banker. If the banker runs out of money you have won, but the reverse is also true. Published in The Assassins releases as well as 3138 Rob's Hot Games #2, 17 Bit Software compilations and was a coverdisk for Amiga Action #60 in August 1994.

214590.overview: As a world-class shopper, you will only buy items that are on sale. Your local store has 45 Blue-light specials on sale an d it is your job to find as many as you can and get them to the checkout counter. The problem is, the other shoppers in the store are all maniacs who will knock you down and steal your purchases. Get as many of the sale items to the checkout counter as you can. If you can score all 45, you are indeed a WORLD CLASS SHOPPER!

214591.overview: Shuffle Run is a game for two players created by Benjamin Stegemann as Paradise Soft and released as freeware in 1992.  You need to insert a joystick in both game ports !!  Player one uses the joystick in port two, player two the one in port one. The game has a built in level editor.

214592.overview: A contribution to the Mekka Symposium 97 32k game competition, coded by Axel G with graphics by Syntic and Sultan. The game is a Space Invaders style game. It was also released on the Disk 9377 compilation disk.

214593.overview: An updated, yet simplified version of the Milton Bradley Simon electronic game created by Richard "DawnBringer" Fhager. This is one of the oldest game ideas there is, repeat the sequence of lights and sounds. The game will have 100 levels. Use arrow keys to repeat sequences, the sequence is played faster by each level.

214594.overview: A recreation of the Simon electronic memory game from Milton Bradley, created by Claudio Buraglio of Pyratronic.

214595.overview:
Skarabeusz is a Polish computer adaptation of Scrabble for up to four players, played on a 15x15 grid board. Each player starts the round with seven letters, which may be replaced or placed on the board. Each letter has a certain value. For an arranged word, the player receives as many points as located on the letters forming the word. Each color on the board has a special characteristics causing doubling or tripling points for letters or arranged words.

As a free bonus, Masa Krytyczna and Kości zostały rzucone are added in the box.

214596.overview: A Skat game based on the official rules of the German Skat Association. Different types of play are supported such as Regelskat, Bierlachs or Ramsch.

214597.overview: A beat'em up from Simon Mitchen aka Gadge of Gadge Software, released in 1996.

214598.overview: A remake of a C64 game created in 1983 called Ski, this version was published by Courbois Software. The premise will feel familiar, get down the slalom by going between as many gates as possible, jump and dodge obstacles and get the best time possible. Consecutive gates increase your score. Fast skiers will progress to the new stages.

214599.overview: A single player Amiga update and remake of Time Fighter for the Italian market, created by Luca Missora and released in 1988.

214600.overview: A sliding puzzle game from Only Games, this is the sequel to the original Slide It, Slide It II was released in 1992 with familiar gameplay but all new timed puzzles to stump your brain.

214601.overview: A shareware slide and match game with increased difficulty caused by "magnets" that lock pieces in place, so careful where you slide! Created by Only Games and released in 1990.

214602.overview: The classic 15 puzzle slider game created in teak and marble by W. Petermann with automatic shuffle, a configurable board size, demonstration solutions and a timer to show your best solution speed.  Slider is a Puzzle game, published by Cachet, which was released in Europe in 1988 and in North America in 1991.

214603.overview: Sliding Skill is a Puzznic variant. In each of the hundred levels the goal is to destroy all movable blocks by sliding them into each other. As soon as a block is moved into a direction, it moves until it meets an obstacle. Blocks can only be pushed so it is important to plan ahead. Of course there are obstacles (e.g. moving walls, tiles which break away after being stepped on or the time limit) and power ups (e.g. a sucker to get a stone out of a bad position) which influence the gameplay.

214619.overview: Smash TV which used to be a popular arcade game has also been ported to the Amiga by the company Ocean. A fan of the game has also written this SEUCK based version which some believe is more playable than the Ocean Port. If you liked the arcade version then give this a go.  For those of you who never played Smash TV it is basically a futuristic game show where the contestants have to fight to the death to win prizes.

214620.overview: A single player collect em up game where the goal is to pick up all the diamonds without retracing any of your steps and before time runs out. Created by Andre Voget and Johannes Selback for Peter Keim Software and released in 1991. The game was released with full source code.

214621.overview:
I made this in 95/96. so it doesn't represent my work today. It was my first "big" idea/project and later based on another game on aminet which involved controlling your "car" on a few coloured tracks.The game was playable, but it lacked versatility mainly because it was turned based.  My "clone" is real time and uses 16 colors, but has just 2 players. the tracks you can select have different filename Prefixes(before filename) which means,

race:
E - an easy track
M - a mediocre track (average)
H - a hard track
misc:
F - a fun track
T - a test track , to test new combinations and drawings
B - a bad track. u cant reach finish,
    or my code doesn't handle the track the way its supposed to be
TUTORIAL - for beginners or when representing a new palette
I - a track with useful info or other miscellaneous things

214623.overview: An updated version of the seminal classic action collect'em up game by P. Hubert and released to public domain in 1988.

214624.overview:
Snake Pit is a Snake game in the style of Nibbler where the player has to guide his munching reptile through a maze full of food pellets. The aim is to eat all the pellets and then one or several exits will open up. The problem is that the snake body grows with every eaten pellet which makes it harder to find a path through the labyrinths without colliding with own body which leads to a lost life. A difference from other Snake games is that touching walls does not lead to death. Instead the player loses points and after a short while the snake will randomly choose a new direction to move in. In addition to normal pellets there are also those that shrink the snake when eaten. There are also special walls that can be pushed around by the snake as long as there is nothing on the opposite side of it.

The game has fifty levels and it's possible to start them in any order without completing the previous ones. Also included is a built in editor that allows the player to edit the levels. The editor works similar to a paint program with the player drawing walls and pellets on the screen.

214625.overview: A freeware game from NC. Games for one or two players. This is a worm\snake game naturally, pick up the randomly placed numbers in order and avoid eating your own tail. The game has 20 levels to slither past.

214626.overview: A Snake\Worm variant created by Harald Müller (Mueller) and released to the wild in 1994.

214627.overview: An AMOS freeware game created by Martijn Stam and Dennis van Koningsbruggen for Dimensions Software. The game title is the developers name backwards. It was released in 1995 and came with a built in level editor. Once upon a time in a country very, very near, there was a tragedy going on. The evil king Commodore had gone mad and wanted to destroy his only daughter, princess Amiga. Helped by his evil slaves, the liquidators, king Commodore is going to make a BIG MISTAKE. So it is time for you, prince Pleasance, to go to the castle in Maidenhead and defeat the evil ones. In the castle you will come across many dangers, as the king has turned his castle into a fortress. But with quick thinking, fast action, power ups and some bravery you will reach your beloved princess just in time! And if you need any help with the quest, prince Proudfoot is there to help you. Good luck, you will need it!

214628.overview:
The kids from a rival town are invading! You and your snowball skills are all that is standing in their way. Try to score the highest as wave after wave of enemies appear! There may be a polar bear or two as well...

Use joystick 2 to move left and right. Press and hold the fire button between the trees to build a snowball. You can build small, medium and large. Push up on the joystick when you are below a snowball to throw it. The larger the snowball, the more damage or does. You get more points for hitting further away enemies.

Good luck in the Snow Wars!

214629.overview: A collection of five solitaire games: Carlton; Martha; Pas Seul; Slider; and Poker Squares. Doubled as a demo for SERIOUS SOLITAIRE and published on Assassins Game disk #93.

214630.overview: Solit aka Solitaire is a freely-distributable, shareware non-Klondike solitaire card game for the Amiga by Felix R. Jeske, it runs under Workbench 2.x. This is version 1.13 which contains some enhancements to version 1.06 found on FF882. There were two versions, the demo and a full version with extra features like undo and so forth.

214631.overview: A collection of card games released in 1997 by Leon Pennington. It includes Klondike, Pyramid, Beleauered Castle, ST Helana, Calculation, Miss Milligan, Scorpion, Demon and Windmill variants.

214632.overview: A homebrew adaptation of the Parker Brothers, Sorry! board game released in 1990 for 4 players. This is the computer version of an old Parker board game from 1934. Also suitable for social gatherings.

214633.overview: A slide puzzle game like a 15 puzzle but with an 8x8 board, luckily there is no time limit. The game was created by the prolific game creator, Harald Müller (Mueller) and published in 1995.

214634.overview: A shareware strategy game for up to four players that can be played in total versus mode or in cooperative teams by Raymond Saltel and released in 1995. Set up curved space, planets, nebula and asteroids, black holes, time limited turns, hit probability and if ships can exit the map. Define your ship, equip with weapons and propulsion.

214635.overview: A scrolling vertical Shoot 'Em Up created by Dimmen Gestel who did coding, graphics and music for this game,  released to the public domain in 1989.

214636.overview: An asteroids clone\update made by Harald Müller (Mueller) and released commercially in 1994.

214637.overview: A Space Invaders clone of exceptional fidelity created by Havie in 2000.

214638.overview: The final release in the Space Invasion series, the 3.0 version was release, this time as Freeware in 1998. This time it is a more minimalistic setup, but with barriers. With this 1998 version, it seems the author tried to stay closer to the 1978 arcade game, with it no longer being a commercial release that became somewhat easier.

214639.overview: An endless asteroids dodging game from Marten Wobst aka Goldmomo with graphics by Arboris, with tagline of "You will not survive". There is no shooting in this 2021 homebrew game, you must simply maneuver, doge and survive. You have a shield of limited power that will take some of the brunt of a glancing contact with the asteroid field but it won't last forever. Hiscore is saved after game exit (unprotect your floppy disk if used).

214640.overview: A much more complex and updated Lunar Lander \ "balloon in the caves" style reaction and navigation game. It has 10 levels repeating at increased levels of difficulty.

214641.overview: A homebrew port and modification of the Taito game Space Invaders to the Amiga with a change from the original space aliens to the card-suite formed baddies the name implies.

214642.overview:
"Spades" is a program written to play the card game Spades. It may be run from the CLI or the Workbench. This is a one player version of Spades -- you play one hand, and the computer plays your partner and two opponents. The program plays by the following rules adopted by my friends and I here at the University of South Florida:

     1) Four players are found, divided into two partnerships of two players each. Partners sit opposite each other. 
     2) A dealer is randomly picked. Each player receives 13 cards from a standard 52-card deck dealt clockwise starting with the player on the dealer's left. On successive hands, the deal passes to the left.
     3) Starting to the left of the dealer, each player bids the number of tricks he feels his hand can take. Bidding passes clockwise. A partnership's bid is the total of the two partners' bids. A partnership must take this total number of tricks.
     4) Play starts with the player to the left of the dealer and passes clockwise. The only rule about leading is that spades may not be lead until spades have been broken (i.e., played during a hand), unless a player holds only spades.
     5) Players must follow suit -- if you have a card of the suit lead, you must play it. Otherwise, any suit may be played. Play ends with the player to the right of the leader. In other words, each player plays one card.
     6) Highest card of the suit lead, or highest spade if a spade has been played, wins the trick. Cards rank 2 lowest through Ace highest. The trick
winner scores one trick for his partnership and then leads for the next trick.
     7) After all 13 tricks in a hand have been taken, scores are totaled. If a partnership takes at least as many tricks as they bid, they get 10 points for each trick they bid and one point for each trick they took over their bid. If a partnership fails to take the number of tricks they bid, they lose 10 points for each trick they bid. If NIL bids are in effect, and a player bid zero tricks and took zero, his side scores 100 points. If a player bid zero and took at least one trick, his side loses 100 points. If Bags are in effect, and a team has accumulated 10 or more overtricks, they lose 100 points. Negative scores are possible.
     8) Deal passes to the left for another hand. First team to 500, or the team with the highest score if both cross 500, wins.

214643.overview: Originally released as shareware, this shooter from Mark Sheeky of Scorpius Software was eventually deemed shareware on his old website and can be found on Assassin Game Disk #91. Shoot your way through the walls until you have enough room to fly through.

214644.overview: A Centipede clone created by Harald Müller (Mueller) and released by Intersoft in 1994. This one moves fast so I hope you are up to it!

214645.overview: Try to order colored balls in horizontal or vertical rows to remove them and got points for it. Different sound fx and sets of balls / stones. Bonusround if all cleared. Only playable with joystick. Also a very first game coded in AMOS 1.3, no compiler avail at it’s time, starts from workbench by calling RAMOS.

214646.overview: This game is an adaptation of the solitaire 'arachnid' for WINDOWS, or 'spider' for Sun/Openwin game.

214647.overview: Basically move from side to side and up and down to avoid the cursor and shoot an enemies, for no score, and survive. Released as a part of Assassins Disk 207. The game is set in WWII. You are flying on a mission with your squadron, but your wingman and your fellow flyers were shot down. You must get back to England alone. Avoid the enemy target sites behind you and shoot planes for energy bonuses.

214648.overview: This is a German version of Battleship where you play against the computer, a conversion of the classic board game. The player plays against the computer. Each has fleet of ships placed on a grid and must fire (blindly) at the enemy in the hope of hitting their ships. The first player to sink all enemy ships wins the game.

214649.overview: A single-player mind board game roughly based on Othello by Peter Varga of Atlantis Software. A normal or a timed game options are available.

214650.overview: A game released by Kain for the Gamedev competition Ludum Dare 40. Your goal is to walk through levels without touching anything. You can get a better score by gathering bonus squares. Beware - if they touch anything you will lose them! Also, there is a nightmare mode, which will kill you if any square touches anything.

214651.overview: A board game published by Markt & Technik in 1991 along with Dex and Tile and later released as part of an Astronut & Wise man compilation. Additionally, released on Power-Disc 5.

214652.overview: A one or two player shareware Tetris game created by Zeth Ward and Ben Brown of Spunout Software and released in 1997.

214654.overview: Squigs is a video game published in 1993 on Amiga. It's an action and puzzle game, set in an arcade, falling block puzzle and tile matching puzzle themes. It was published in Amiga Power Magazine.

214655.overview: An unofficial conversion of the C64 game of the same name. You are a Pac Man type creature and you must move about various mazes collecting 250 eggs that the Queen Squirm is laying before her workers collect them. As you move about you also need to look out for a small glow worm which needs collecting because after a short time the lights go out and you can't see the maze but you can see the Squirm's. Touch a Squirm or the Queen and you lose one of three lives. Once you have collected 200 eggs you have a bonus run where you move about the maze leaving a tail and you try to move about before you touch your tail. The maze is viewed from above and the whole maze is on one screen and two players can play taking it in turns when one player dies. A joystick or keyboard can be used to control your character.

214656.overview:
Star Chess is a German language board game, developed and published by Media GmbH, which was released in Europe in 1995. The chess program
with new ideas! StarChess not only uses the classic methods to calculate a move, but also uses new methods that are constantly being further developed. StarChess has particular strengths, especially in the positional STARI game. It's not just a "tactical piece-swapping program," but strives to use a good positional tactics to achieve the most promising possible endgame situation. Because more than 90% of all chess games are decided in the endgame phase, when there are only very few pieces left on the board attention was paid to modularity, especially in the opening phase.
The opening library can be expanded almost limitlessly without having to replace the entire program. So you can easily add new libraries or remove existing ones. Therefore, special opening archives will follow in the near future. The first additional library to appear will deal in great detail with the "English" and the "Morra Gambit" opening. And that's very simple: copy the opening file into the "Moduls" drawer, and that's it! The program includes the opening automatically. But even in the basic version, StarChess already has a good knowledge of openings.

214657.overview:
Steel Devils is an action game published by German company Wolf Software & Design via their label Oase Software. The game is an arena fighter where two mechs try to destroy each other. There is no single player mode, only two human players can play against each other at the same time.
The game uses a top-down view. Players compete in an arena which consists of a single screen. There are 20 different arenas to choose from. Each arena has a different layout with indestructible obstacles. Power-ups will appear randomly on screen. These include temporary invisibility, several weapons, mines or health supply. A player is destroyed once his health is drained. Then the other player scores a point and the duel starts anew, until one player has reached a pre-set number of points.

214658.overview: Steinschlag is a Tetris like game (Steinschlag means "Falling Rock") submitted by the author. This is version 1.8, an update to version 1.5 from Fish disk 221 from 1989. This version was published in Fish Disk #238.

214659.overview: A PD horse betting game created by Tiger Software and released in 1993. You can inspect the stables to get some info. Then pick a horse, bet on it and then watch the race to see if you won! You can also buy a stable and own your own horses if you want to dig deeper in to the game.

214660.overview: Drop the sets of three colors, you can change the order as they drop. Try to get sets of 3 or more that will disappear to free space. You lose when your pile of colors reaches the top. It is a game we've seen before, but this one has a few surprises.

214661.overview: A solitaire game from Harald Müller (Mueller) published commercially in 1995, it could be set to use English or German and would be later republished in Gamers' Delight 2 compilation.

214662.overview: Strateq is like an enhanced version of Chess for two players. It is even more complex than Tactrix!, which is also found here in AmiNet.   Strateq includes 14 different pieces, which have a fully-functional hit-point system. A multitude of different features are also included.   Strateq was written in AMOS and requires at least 1 MB of total memory. The instructions are now in AmigaGuide format.

214663.overview:
An implementation of the "Streets and alleys" patience, and its variation "Beleaguered castle", where you have eight shuffled stacks of cards surrounding four pads where cards of the same colour must be stacked from the ace and upwards. Cards can be moved between stacks, but only adjacent numbers.

The game is multitasking-friendly and has settings for screen colours, hints and can talk to you using voice synthesis.

214664.overview: Strikeball is a version of baseball with a few rule changes. You can set the number of innings played. Pitching you can determine fast, slow or medium pitch. Field with outfield and shortstop, bases cannot run, only throw.  You get credit for each base taken as a run, home runs are given 5 runs. If a fielder tags the base before the running he is out, but gets credit for each base already touched. Fielders must throw to bases, cannot tag the runner out themselves. Released on United Public Domain Games disk PG181 and BAB Micro Center Domaine Public No3465.

214667.overview: An updated version of the Sea Battle component of Atari's Air-Sea Battle created as Shareware by Perry Rosenboom and released in 1991.

214668.overview: Sudden Death is a classic 2 player or 4 player tron style game. Built-in instructions for making your own levels. The object of the game is to avoid the light cycles trial and try to kill the other players. If you crash, you lose.

214669.overview: A two player variant of Tetris, created with AMOS and released with source code and bundled with AMOS Professional. The game was created by Dominic Ramsey, while technically the game was freeware it came as part of the game creation packaging.

214670.overview: Created by  Conan Mcphee of Katzma in the spring of 1996 as a public domain game, this is a Freeway\Frogger variant action game. As Darryl, you have to prove to your pea-brained peers that you're no chicken. How? By being unreasonably stupid - by running back and forth on the M-11 to core maximum points! Use the joystick to get from one side to the other as many times as possible and grab bonus points by picking up the Golden Katzma statues. See if you can discover Darryl's secret move. If you can, try to work out how to save the almost certainly doomed hedgehog....good luck!

214671.overview: A one or two player, freeware Worm\Snake style game created by Anders Persson aka di3andpe, the original was written in the style of Nibbles, this new version allowed better graphics, new music and more monsters, built-in track editor, more levels and hard drive installable and with an English translation.

214672.overview: A colorful four reel fruit\slot machine created by Gary Hunt in 1994 with 15 adjustable skill levels. Released as PDWare on GM126.

214673.overview: A single player video poker game also known as Power Poker and created by Harald Müller (Mueller) and released in 1995.

214674.overview: A one or two player billiards style game created by Malcolm Bamber and released to PD in 1992, you will have no problems sinking balls as the felt will be full of them. Every space on the sides of the felt is covered with pockets, not just the usual six. The challenge is that you can never reuse a pocket and it is incredibly easy to accidentally put the cue ball into a pocket.

214676.overview: A Skiddy kart style racing game with no single player mode, in it you race against a friend as  . It has a mini game on title screen similar to Pong from Super Skidmarks. Super Skiddy 3 - Things on Ice is from Simon Hitchen of Gadge Software.  It's a 2 player racing game (on ice).  There are 4 tracks and there are 3 levels to how icy it is.

214677.overview: A single player Tetris clone (with badgers) created by Dale Norton using AMOS and released to Public Domain as a demo in 1992.

214678.overview: A two player Pong game, brought up to the times in this 1993 release. Featuring interesting space themed backgrounds a asteroid that bounces between the top and the bottom of the playing field, deflecting balls in unexpected ways and power ups and other surprises. The game was created by Anjam Sarwar and Mohammed Iqbal and was published on the Assassins CD02 Ultimate Games collection.

214679.overview: A single player action game where you need to avoid the 2 baddies and gather up the items. Kind of an acid trip Pac-Man with a puzzle element released in 1989 by Tee Djay.

214680.overview:
Welcome to Super Tron 97 by S.O.S. This version is freeware. We hope you will enjoy the game.

This version took 3 days to finish. In 1993, I Beast released Super Tron for Amiga at The Computer Cross Road in Göteborg. Your mission is avoid colliding with yourself, walls or opponent and make your opponent collide with your light cycle tail, walls, or other items. 

While early versions were a 1-2 player game. Amiga Version 1.2 is for 1-4 Players.

214681.overview: A Tron\Worm\Lightcycle game released as Shareware by Beast  and Dalos of Sfinx Productions. It can be configured to have no walls, easy, normal, hard or ARE YOU NUTS? difficulty levels for two players, naturally. It was released in Pinion Pack 2 compilation and in the Diamonds And Pearls 4 compilation pack.

214682.overview: A German language super gambler casino game put out by Fairware in 1992 and published by Schatztruhe in 1992 and Rasputin Software starting in 1994. Released in the compilation Super Zocker/Blackjack II release.

214683.overview:
Syman is a simple and fun memory game for all the family, playable by up to four people simultaneously. Syman is based on the original MB 'Simon' game, with inspiration drawn from the American Dad tv series, and is produced by a small team here at Ultimate Amiga. Simply watch the coloured tones played by Syman, and play them back.

The game was started from scratch on 12/12/09 with the goal of being finished in time for the Underground Arcade Christmas Competition which closed on Christmas Eve 2009.

214684.overview:
Syzyf is a timed puzzle-solving game, similar to Sokoban. The task requires making a passage to the evacuation point. There are two types of ground: standard and ice. Ice ground slides the vehicle to the first standard ground field. The cubes are divided into four types, two movable and two immobile. The first one moves just one field after pushing, the second one stops after contact with any obstacle, the third one may be only destroyed be using a bomb and the fourth one can't be removed at all. There are three types of vehicle visualization. The vehicle may carry an unlimited amount of bombs.

The game consists a total of 80 levels. After each completed level the player receives a password. The game features a level editor for up to 15 boards.

214685.overview: A game built on the addictive game PONGO but with several added features.  You have been assigned the demanding task of cleaning viruses from your SYSOP's hard disk. To kill a virus, you simply kick a disk at it. There are fifty different levels, and on each level, the speed will increase and the viruses will be smarter and start to hunt you. Version 2.10, binary only.

214757.overview: A single player freeware poker game created by Richard Bonny in AmigaBasic. Also released as part of the "50 Great Games" compilation by Wicked Software in 1991 under the title "Space Poker".

214889.overview: A homebrew remake of Spy Hunter by fibble42 released in 2022. It is an Arcade top down Action vehicle game that drew its inspiration from James Bond, this version written using Earok's Scorpion Engine!. As a super agent you must drive for your life in a turbo-charged car that is equipped with the most current weapon technology. The street is full of hostile agents, that have nothing else in mind than to atomize you and your engineering marvel. Manoeuvre your car at highest speed and with all your abilities, but watch out for the "Road Lord", the "Switch Blade", the "Enforcer" and the other hostile agents that will try to hold you back on land and water. You have to destroy them before they eliminate you.

214894.overview: A fantastically accurate conversion for the classic Sramble arcade game for the Amiga 500 and above by Jean-François Fabre aka JOTD or jotd666, released as a freeware game in 2022. A two player version was added after the initial release.  You play as a spaceship and must fly through tight caves and over landscapes, while being attacked by launched rockets, ufo's and other such nasties without ending up having your ship blown into smithereens. If you can avoid or destroy these hazards and not run out of fuel, you should be able to reach the end stage and destroy the enemy base.

214948.overview: A reverse engineered modification by Philippe Guichardon (Meynaf). Based on 1986 Atari Games coin-op; Amiga version ported from 1986 State of the Art/Electric Dreams Atari ST release. Like the original ST version, Super Sprint is a racing game for one or two players. Gameplay is from an overhead view of the racetrack. The racetracks start simple and gradually get more complicated, and may also feature obstacles ranging from traffic cones to tornadoes. Occasionally wrenches will appear in the roadway, and when collected they can be used after a race to power up your car with better tires, better acceleration or a higher top speed.

214950.overview: A Spodland game created by Martin Fox and Andrew Crowe and released as Manta Soft in 1997. Shoot at the other Spodz, certain combinations will cause your shots to impact shots from others and not make it to target. Take down the others to win. Several levels to choose from and choose the tracker mod file you want to listen to as you take down your enemies.

214953.overview: Described as a gymnasium party vs game, this version of Space Taxi has a lot of little tricks, like landing on top of each other and pushing each other into walls. The programmers made it very simple to replace the music, so you can have your own version of Space Taxi with your own music. There are a lot of levels including a black hole level, a level in which the controls are reversed in certain regions, a level where your thrusters stop functioning in certain places, a level where a bubble follows you until you land, levels with switches and moving elevator platforms, a level that is completely dark until you see a lightning flash that illuminates the platforms, a level with the bullets from jump man that shoot at you, and tons more!

214968.overview:
Snakeman is a public domain Oil's Well style game. The idea is to extend a snake down into a maze to collect 'dots'. The body of the snake extends into the maze, and this can't be crossed over, however you may retract the snake in order to take a different route through the maze or to avoid enemies. Should an enemy make contact with your snake, you lose a life. A level is cleared by collecting all the dots in it. Bonus items are scattered around the levels, which reward the player with extra time, points or lives if collected.

Snakeman was programmed in the AMOS programming language.

215006.overview: A top-down racing game which allows you to race C5's around a track, against a friend or computer or even on your own in time trial mode. Who needs fast formula 1 racing when you can race a three speed plastic C5 around the track? The game features a flat battery mode for 2 players only, and fastest lap/race times and championship tables are all automatically saved. A track editor is enclosed.

215017.overview: An action football game with a heavy slice of management released in German and English markets known variously as Samba World Cup and Samba World Cup 98 (and possibly Samba 3 World Cup?), supporting both AGA and ESC video and created by  Jo Seitz, Emmanuel Henné with music by Jochen Heizmann (Joe Heizmann), it was unfortunately released a little too late to coincide with the France '98 Tournament as they failed to get the FIFA endorsement or sanction. But while it looks a bit too much like USA '94 it does have lots of goodies: sampled speech, throw ins, free kicks and penalty shots.

215018.overview: Sir Losealot was reviewed in Amiga Format Issue #117 (December 1998) and was included on the Cover CD (AFCD33). Created in the Aspire 2 Game Engine. A 2D scrolling, multi directional platform collector.

215019.overview:
Remake of the game Soko Ban released in 1982 and presented at AmiGameJam21 . Coded in AMOS, this is the first tukinem game.

The game has 53 levels. There are three display modes to choose from: CGA, Tandy, and Amiga. Soko-Ban is a classic puzzle game, the basis of many clones in recent years. It is installed in a warehouse. At each level, the player must push crates (from square to square) to bring them to the designated places; once each crate is in a marked location, the level is complete. Crates can only be pushed one at a time (so two side-by-side crates can't be pushed together) and can't be pulled - so it's possible to get a crate stuck in a corner, where it can't be recovered! At the later levels, you need to plan 40 stages in advance. 

Updates in 2022 added Dual Playfield and high scores.

215021.overview: The sequel to the original Defender style horizontally scrolling shooter created by Harald Müller (Mueller) and prequel to Space Bomber 3. Save the humans and destroy the aliens. It would be later re-released in the Gamers' Delight and Gamers' Delight 2 compilations.

215022.overview: A Defender style shooter complete with a scanner and humans to rescue. It was made by Harald Müller (Mueller) and published by Intersoft, which was released in Europe in 1993.

215024.overview: The final release in the set of Space Bomber games from coder : Harald Müller (Mueller), all published in 1993 and released in Germany. It is a 2D, horizontally scrolling Defender style game. Save the humans on the ground from the aliens in the air.

215025.overview: A version of Space Invaders created by Kev Gallagher  without the protective barriers normally found in the game, with major versions in 1993 and 1998. The 1993 version was published by Towerbyte Software, while the 1998 version is truer to the original, save the lack of barriers.

215026.overview:
An updated version of Space Invaders for the Amiga by Kevin Gallagher and released in 1994. Kev has made several versions of this game, this one is marked Space Invasion II and features the 4 barriers at the bottom that provide cover for your ship...for a time. Red Alert! The invaders are attacking! Your mission is to kill the invading alien scumbags before they invade earth. Use your moue or joystick to control your lazer and waste as many of the blighters as you can. This version also features 50 invaders per level. 
 
It was also published in IDG Media's Amiga Action Issue #69, Cover Disk 2.

215042.overview:
WARNING THIS GAME CONTAINS CRUDE HUMOUR & IS NOT INTENDED FOR CHILDREN OR ANYONE EASILY OFFENDED. It is a text adventure with some graphics for the Holiday Season. This little game has been put together for the First Annual Festive Amiga Games Competition. The game itself is based on Telltale Games' Sam & Max Nearly Save Christmas and Ice Station Santa.

It uses backgrounds and sprites downscaled from Telltale's concept art and the Lucasarts title Sam & Max Hit the Road.  Sam and Max themselves are the creation of Steve Purcell. Enjoy and don't judge the game too harshly as it was put together in a holiday rush and wrapped up in a bow for you to enjoy. MERRY CHRISTMAS TO ALL!!

215050.overview: A freeware Arkanoid clone..this time with adult content that would be exposed as the bricks are removed or as it is told, there are "...naked chicks behind the bricks!" This game has MATURE CONTENT.

215051.overview: A sequel to the original freeware Arkanoid clone with adult content for MATURE AUDIENCES, where the models are exposed as the bricks are removed or as it is told, there are "...naked *Hollywood* chicks behind the bricks!". This is not a game mod where the pictures have been replaced by a third party, it is made by the original creators.

215054.overview: Sexy 2 is a multi screen 2D platformer game, developed and published by DoubleByte and created with AMOS, which was released in Europe in 1992. MATURE CONTENT AND IMAGES.

215081.overview: You were at a loss at what to do next. Just then an old man started talking to you. "Spekkio is the god of battle. Try your strength. You have all the time in the world!" In each level, your objective is to find an exit before your 3 lives run out. In specific levels, you must defeat (or escape) enemy bosses.

215116.overview: An overhead, single-screen 2D basic racing game created by Cyberstyle and released in 1990. Ok to practice as a single racer, there are no computer racers, but better to play with a friend. A single championship with four tracks.

215125.overview:
Szachista is an adaptation of classic Chess game for up to two players (human or computer). The game allows to set a few additional visual options presented in adjustable windows, such as a list of defeated pawns, real-time movement analysis or turn clock. The player may use hints, undo last move, select of of three available difficulty levels. The database of the game includes most of the known Chess tactics showing the name of the recognized ones.
The game has a built-in tutorial explaining all Chess rules and allowing to practice prepared tasks.

215128.overview: A pinball game by Power Project for Amiga modeled on the classic Pinball Wizard released in the same year of 1987, all the sound fx are the same, the playing fields and high score tables have the same layout, a loading music loop is included and there's even a weird result when you try to soft re-set the Amiga just like Pinball Wizard. Has some racy backgrounds so a mature user warning may be in order.

215130.overview: A puzzle game that is a clone of Atomix. Game design by Tunç Dindaş and Cem Tanik. Coding by Cem Tanik. Graphics by Tunç Dindaş; level design by Dursun Turunç. The game came with 50 levels, though buggy operation often left the user with far less playable levels. It was developed by Zombie Boys and published by Sultan Soft, which was released in Europe in 1994. On each level, you are given a couple of atoms, and your task is to arrange them into a specific molecule or shape within a given, limited time frame.

215131.overview: A head to head version of Tetris coded in AMOS and released as licenseware by David Shattu of Polygon Software.

215133.overview: Created by Ken Vale of Antimax Software and released in 1992, this single player multi-directional shooter has you piloting a space fighter taking out baddies all over this space station complex.

215134.overview: Made by Gore Design, Dark Energy and Sky of Energy , this Public domain, 4-player homebrew was released in 1993.

215135.overview:
Sid was out walking in the country when suddenly a strange doorway appeared and dragged him away. Sid found himself in total darkness. He seemed to be floating and could not move. Suddenly and odd looking sphere rolled towards him. A deep voice spoke out: "Sidney, you are the chosen one. You have been selected to save the planet Skan-29 from the evil droids that have stolen it. Due to the intense gravity, you must use this spherical ship to move about. Destroy the five evil droids and you may return to your own planet. Fail and the droids will be powerful enough to rule the whole universe... 
 
Sid did not want to save a planet that he had never heard of, but there didn't seem much choice.  
 
A platform game made in Amos by Jedi Productions where you avoid dangers and collect coins. It was released in 1992.

215136.overview: Sirius 7 is an horizontally scrolling shooter game, developed by Art Computer Software and published by CRL, which was released in Europe in 1990.

215155.overview: An unreleased 2D multi-directional shooter in the style of Thrust or Gravitar created by coder : Johannes Lipp and musician : Holger Kral in 1991. It is a game in which you look to play as a strange looking sphere that has to traverse a pixelated maze while shooting at things and avoiding crashing into the sides. According to Amiga Games that Weren't ,Slez was one of three games developed by Johannes Lipp including Denjoy and Pot, and would most likely have been seen on German disk magazines (where a game is accompanied by a mini magazine) if released.

215167.overview: A form of Tetris where you must use the provided shapes to fill the gaps in the jumble of blocks below and clear the lines below before playing normally. It was created by Goergen Mirko and released to public domain in 1990.

215168.overview: Released as both a single level demo and a fully functional, shareware multi level beat'em up game by Sandro Marzo of Meditation in 1993. In it you must fight any who stand in your path, visit the mountains an shrines and back-kick your foes in the tranquil forest locations, amongst the butterflies and birdsong.

215237.overview: Speedway Manager is a very simplified management game of the Polish speedway league. The main task of the player is winning the championship by appropriate selection of the team composition for each match day. The are no other management features, such as finances, transfers or stadium expansion. The match window shows all fifteen races with points stats. The driver is described by average score points in the match.

215241.overview: An interactive Christmas themed slideshow and puzzle with paintings of the late Terry Redlin (1937-2016). This is a Commodore Amiga demo "Shuffling Around the Christmas Tree" from Desire. It was released at Syntax 2021 party and was ranked second in the oldskool demo competition.

215243.overview:
Skarbnik is a Polish language adventure game with FPP graphics. The goal of the game is to solve the mystery of the strange events in the Silesian mines. The adventure begins when one of the sidewalks collapsed trapping the player in an old unknown mine shaft. By using the artifacts scattered in the mine the player must find a way out and documents explaining the current events. Besides of solving the puzzles the player will face several enemies, such as a robot with laser eyes, guard with the machine gun or dangerous rats. The enemies may be defeated by using the appropriate items - lack of the items or too late usage may result in loss of energy or death. The player may carry up to four items at a time. The game features a lot of useless objects. Once combined items can't be disconnected, thrown objects disappear forever.

The game is presented in first person perspective, with rendered animated graphics. The control is done with the mouse by using the direction arrows or one of the action icons (take, leave, combine, open, close).

215260.overview: A 12 level demo puzzle game from Arkanix Labs with some colors safe and others could do anything from destroy you to give you a special move. You must reach the exit to get to the new level.

215268.overview:
Speedway Manager 2 is a management game of the Polish speedway league for up to four players. The main task of the player is the appropriate financial management of the club and win the championship.

Income comes only from tickets, advertisements, radio and TV transmissions. The expenditure includes the purchase of motorcycles and tires, salaries of players and spending on gasoline. The match window shows all the races with points stats and allows to make a substitution. The player may turn on the top down side scrolling match animations. The driver is described by average score points in the match.

215316.overview: An attempt to make a version of Tetris that would subvert the current methods of play by having a larger play area and incorporating new piece types that together would force Tetris players to change play style and keep the game fun.

215322.overview:
A top-down vertically scrolling 2D shooter created by Martin Ludwig and Sebastian Ulrich of Cachet and published by Rainbow Arts in Europe in 1988.

Also known as Revenge of Doom.

215362.overview:
Scheduled for release in 1999 by Blittersoft, SPACE STATION 3000 was cancelled in late 2000 after 2.5 years of development for Amiga/PC by developer Digital Images. Space Station 3000 - Features

Space Station is a brand new Strategy Game for PC & Amiga which combines Space Combat and Money Management with other, newer, gaming concepts in order to create a Space Trading Experience somewhat different to any other you may have played.

The Idea of the Game

Your main goals in this game are to build a Space Station that will stand the test of time. And make money. There are numerous other sub-plots to the game but those two are the game's essence.

What with things being no fun when they're too easy, we've included many obstacles to prevent you reaching your goals, but I'll introduce you to them later.

You start with a small amount of money and a standard, un-expanded Corus Class Space Station and through either hard work, talent and persistence, or underhand tactics and blind luck, you must make a success of your venture.

215375.overview: Welcome to Shankara, the quest for magic stones! Shankara is a single player, overhead 2D-view arcade-adventure game created by Simone Zannotti; it requires an Amiga with: - 3MB Ram, - Hard Disk,- 68020+ and a Joystick. There is a level editor too, for creating new adventures! Find your way into ancient, foreboding pyramids, past traps and dangers untold to find the hidden treasures and mysteries of history.

215377.overview: Ride the wild waves in this horizontally scrolling 2d surfing game. This surfing game was part of a multi-game system (BiffSelect) along with Biff Boardin'. The system includes a board (snowboard or surfboard) that connects to the joyport and 3 games: BIFF BOARDIN, URBAN SURFIN, & BIFF SELECT. Originally intended to be released on the Amiga CD32 and the Amiga line. It is unclear if this was an unreleased prototype or just had a very limited local North American commercial release.

215384.overview:
Thaurus is an adaptation of the Peg Solitaire board game. The game consists of two similar timed modes: Samotnik and Thaurus.

In Samotnik mode the action takes place on a standard board of 45 figures. All figures are the same and cover all fields except the middle one. The main task is to remove as many figures as possible, leaving only one at best. The pawns are removed by translating them in horizontal or vertical direction. The game ends when there is no possibility of movement. The result depends on the number of pawns remaining on the board.

Thaurus mode uses same rules but is much harder, as it introduces a special field (or fields) where the last remaining pawn (or pawns) should stay at the end. Before each new board player receives a level password.

215391.overview: A 1 or 2 player sports Football/Soccer management game from Sayonara Software, created by Jo Seitz and released in 1996.

215493.overview:
Additional information from the coder József Punk: "Stalker is a prototype of an Amiga game I developed with two of my friends about 20 years ago.
The main unique feature of the game was the rearrangeable playfield. The player controls a two leg robot in a scene that is built by same sized blocks.
These blocks are moveable in rearrange mode. He went on to say, although there are different versions available, the game was never finished nor released as they couldn't find a publisher to finance the development.

215498.overview: An updated version of the game Gyruss, in which you rotate your ship in a pseudo 3d shooter blasting away oncoming enemies.. Or in the case of SVLCVSS D "Boing Balls". The game is currently released as a demo and further work is on hold as of 2022.

215509.overview:
Six short mathematical tests aimed at children up to 7 years of age come together in this package. Sooty the silent magical bear is one of the UK’s most enduring children’s characters, and his friends Sweep the squeaking dog and Soo the talking bear join him here. The games can be played with little or no computer knowledge, and feature full graphics.

In Magic Numbers the player must count how many wands Sooty has on the screen. Sweep’s Bones involves moving bones from a pile on the right (Sweep’s stash) to the left (the ones he will enjoy today). Soo’s Hats is an addition test. In Bigger/Smaller you are presented with 2 numbers, and asked to select the biggest or smallest, which Sooty will magic away with his wand. Order Order presents a line of numbers, some of which are filled in, and challenges the player to select the others (which are randomly arranged elsewhere on the screen) and place them in the correct positions. Soo’s Race brings these skills together – you are asked a succession of questions, and answering them correctly will see Sooty’s car move along a track, and hopefully win its race against Sweep.

215510.overview: A 2D, overhead-view Kart style racing game for up to four players, commercially released in 1998 as part of the ULTIMATE SUPER SKIDMARKS compilation. It is a version of Super Skidmarks with comical sound effects and a bunch of different vehicles. There are a number of circuits provided, all of them with walls around them to ensure crash-bang-wallop racing, and most of them have parts that cross with other parts, making collisions possible if you're much ahead of (or behind) other cars (fortunately there's no car damage). They can be raced forwards or backward - perhaps the first game with this feature available. You could either run single races, or one of the in-built championships - one for each car, across a specially selected set of tracks.

217013.overview: Simple is a Puzzle game, developed and published by (L)egal, which was released in Europe in 1988.

217103.overview:
Your child will learn to spell the fun way with this highly addictive spelling aid with a game like atmosphere to make spelling practice that bit more enjoyable.
The program uses phonics to teach children letter and word recognition, that is to say all words used sound as they spell.
A picture of the word to spell appears on the screen and the child then has to spell the word by clicking with the mouse on the alphabet displayed.
Correct spelling is rewarded by a pleasant tune and a congratulations message.

217104.overview: Spell Bound (1988) is an Educational game, developed and published by Learners Image, which was released in 1988.

217185.overview: Stellaryx is an Asteroids style Shooter game, developed by Vincent Lee and published by Laser Gamesmanship, which was released in Europe in 1988.

217197.overview:
Superhero is a platform Beat'em Up game by Kage that was intended to be available in 1993, a playable demo was released that year as a coverdisk in THE ONE magazine in February 1993. Previewed in CU Amiga, Amiga Joker, and The Games Machine magazines. It was Advertised in Amiga Power issue 23, page 15.
The game was planned for the SNES and MegaDrive too, but the Amiga version was the only one that was completed. Reportedly Full versions were given to reviewers but aside from the demo release it never was distributed.

217256.overview:
Shuriken - a Ninja-themed game based on the arcade classic Berzerk
Built for Amiga OS 3.2 as an entry in the Amiga Blitz Basic Jam 2022

217286.overview: Puzzler based on shape recognition, originally released worldwide in 1990 as part of Gold Disk's AMIGA COMPLETE software compilation only, SILHOUETTE was later published as a budget standalone release in Denmark by Euro Power Pack. In the game you are tested on your ability to identify shapes. There will be six levels to complete. Each level is harder than the last. After the last level you will be compared to some baseline times. The lowest 10 times are saved to disk.

217535.overview: A game which is not only a nod to the disk copy software of X-Copy from back in the day, but it's a block colour matching puzzler shown in this new demo footage from the DECRUNCHparty.
