218089.overview: The sequel to the 2021 Christmas present for the new year! Published in the Amiga Addict issue 17 as the cover disk. Use the Gift-o-matic 5000 to make sure the right presents go to the right homes. No more shooting every present into the chimneys!

218090.overview:
The fan-favourite game of Spike Dodging makes its inevitable journey to the Amiga.
Hold the joystick button (or spacebar, or mouse button) to move along the endless maze of spikes.

218163.overview: Can you help Santa deliver all his presents in time? Avoid the rooftops and shoot those presents into the chimneys and pick up treats for your reindeer along the way, which will give you extra time. Avoid the tempting sherry if you want to go fast, it will slow the game down....though slowing down at Christmas time isn't always a bad thing.

218701.overview: There are four Story So Far compilations, where Vols 1 and 3 were for 16 bit platforms while vols 2 and 4 were for 8 bit platforms. This Amiga compilation contains Battleships, Beyond the Ice Palace, Buggy Boy and Ikari Warriors.

218702.overview: An enjoyable game for all the family with the aim of stopping the bad guys from throwing poor Santa into a pit. It features colorful graphics and Christmas music where we will have to throw gifts at the bad guys to prevent them from climbing to the top of the castle and throwing us into the chasm.

219288.overview:
Sqrxz III is a 2D side-scrolling platformer with a focus on a very high difficulty level. Visually and acoustically the game is resembling platform games from the early 90s. You start the game with 6 lives, but due to tricky passages it's almost impossible to beat even the first level on the first run. In contrast to a few other games (e.g. Eryi's Action) the difficulty is not caused by unforseen traps, but by the need of good reflexes and problem solving skills instead.

Like previous games in the series also this part has some basic back story to it: Our hero Sqrxz is on vacation with his girlfriend Yve, when an "evil power" suddenly kidnaps Yve and forces you to collect all rings spread in the 10 levels - when you missed a ring you will not be able to exit a level. The causes of death are numerous, among others touching spikes or enemies, drowning, being squashed or falling into a pit. When dying you have to restart from the beginning of the level or the last checkpoint - but you do have unlimited continues, with the only penalty loosing your score and having to restart the level from the beginning.

Controls are simplistic: You can only move to the left / right, jump and move slowly. Jumping onto some kinds of enemies will kill or stun them, and basic interaction with the environment is done by touching an item to activate it or pushing a crate to move it.

219289.overview:
The fourth part of the (now) quadrology Jump’n Think series Sqrxz brings you onto an cold icy island. Shiny marbles, evil penguins and ghosts, underwater creatures and many more to expect. Original Sqrxz made by Marcus Vesterlund and John Holmvall. 
 
Features:

* Authentic Retro graphics – Pixels forever!
* 10 die hard levels!
* 11 great tunes!
* Top 10 highscore!
* Unlimited continues!
* Hidden passages!
* Cheat codes! (if you can find them)

219366.overview: A really impressive public domain Star Trek (TOS) game by Eric Gustafson, released in 1988 featuring the sounds, music and pictures from the original television series. You control the crew and determine the status of the ship by looking at it from the perspective of each of the control positions of those crewpeople shown. You can click on Dr. McCoy and see the health status of the crew, click on Spock and see the info he has and so forth. Your mission is to recover stolen information which is vital to the security of the whole Federation. All that Star Fleet could tell you is that, "anywhere from 10 - 15 of these documents are missing". You have under 5 years to complete your mission. Watch out for Klingon & Gorn spies who are also looking for the same information and be wary of the dangers of Tribbles.

219380.overview: A first person exploration game. This is a slow game, so take your time. Find and interact with objects and simply figure things out. Sure, this is not a fully original idea but rather a game I've been trying to make since I was a teenager in one way or another. This time, I have reframed the whole story and character motivation, as well as the puzzles. The level geometry was entirely redone as well, but still bears some vague resemblance with the original concept.

223565.overview: A single player puzzle game from Andreas Turowski with music by Ebsche Hermesmann Junior (EHJ) and released commercially in 1992.

223580.overview:
Settle the World is a turn-based building and trading game with a focus on local multiplayer (up to four players on one Amiga computer).
You will have to found settlements, build roads, establish trade relations with your fellow player, explore the map and sometimes send soldiers to war.

278323.overview: Solius the Sorcerer is a german Amiga multi screen platformer action game released in Europe in 1992 by CompuTec Verlag.

278624.overview: It appears that the fansite SensibleSoccer.de has put together an updated version of the game for Amiga (as spotted by UltimateMister), adding the correct player names and team numbers for the 2022/2023 season. This means you can still enjoy the same fantastic gameplay of the classic Amiga title while also having the benefit of more up-to-date team sheets.

417665.overview: According to the game the strategy for this crosshairs shooter is simple...shoot everything that moves...except the women. The game is divided into a series of levels, which are divided into sub levels, where you need to survive until the timer reaches zero to move on. Of course this gets harder and harder to complete. Watch your ammo supply and avoid shooting "the women".

417667.overview: A shareware racing game for one to 4 competitive players created by Supurb Simulations. In the Feeding Game mode, you select which foods your snail gets to eat in the five days before a race: sugar, crisps, lettuce, cabbage, or apple. I did not understand how the different foods influence the performance of the snail. The manual says it is up to the players to figure that out.

417671.overview:
Soccer Manager Plus is a managerial soccer simulation. The player takes control over a team from the second division and is responsible for its financial and athletic success. In the original German version the game used real athlete and club names, but the athletes are randomly divided between the clubs.

In various menus, the player can set ticket prices, visit a training camp or take action on the transfer market. Before the match, the athletes are divided into the team. Here the player should note each athlete's statistics (goal, defense, offense, mid field and energy) which determine his performance depending on where he is used. The last setting to take is toughness: the higher the setting, the higher the chances of success. The downside is a higher risk of injuries and cards.

The main part of the game is completely menu based, but the player may choose to watch match highlights, only the goals or directly the result. The match segments are shown in a side-scrolling perspective.

417724.overview: A PD\Freeware, single player shooter by Chris Holliman and Clay, released in 1990. Single-screen wave shooter with up to 30 enemies. The game adds one additional enemy per wave until the maximum is reached. The game ends after the energy bar on the right is depleted by collisions with enemies.

418096.overview: This definitely lampoons SimAnt by Maxis from 1992. There is only one action option for the player: Clicking "Exist" summons a brick which crushes the ant below it. "Stats" shows a humorously useless screen with the dimensions of the brick and a few bits of information. Released on Amiga Power issue 13 (May 1992) disk 12B.

418109.overview: A 2D shooter for one player, created by The Pentagon and released in 1989.

418174.overview:
Sensible Soccer, often called Sensi, is an association football video game series which was highly popular in the early 1990s and which still retains a cult following. 
It was developed by Sensible Software and first released for Amiga and Atari ST computers in 1992 as well as for the PC. 
The series was created by Jon Hare and Chris Yates, as a successor to their previous football game MicroProse Soccer (1988), which in turn was inspired by the arcade video game Tehkan World Cup (1985).

It featured a zoomed-out bird's-eye view (the majority of games until then such as Kick Off and Match Day used a closer top-down or side view), editable national, club and custom teams and gameplay utilising a simple and user-friendly control scheme. 
One of the defining gameplay elements was the "aftertouch" feature, which enabled effective but unrealistic swerves. 
The game topped charts such as Amiga Power's "All Time Top 100". The graphic style of the game was used in other Sensible Software games, such as Mega-Lo-Mania, Cannon Fodder and Sensible Golf.

418289.overview: The first in the trilogy of PD\Freeware SEUCK based, vertically scrolling, space shooters. This one supported only one player, where later versions supported 2 player, which only made this difficult to play game even harder.

418290.overview:
This PD\Freeware text adventure game by Davide Bucc is the sequel to The Queen's Footsteps and features an outstanding story line. Today is April 19, 1907. You, Emilia Vittorini, arrived yesterday in Varenna, on the shore of the beautiful Lake Como. You are hosted at the magnificent Villa Briccorosso; Princess Lucilla Briccorosso is preparing the Silk Road Race, a 10,000km rally raid between Cairo in Egypt and Peking in China, to be done by car.

You represent ITA, founded by your father, the company that built the car the Princess just bought to use during the rally. The car is supposed to be delivered today. Your role will be to assist the delivery and make sure everything is perfectly functional.  
 
The game is divided in four parts. When you complete one of them, you will get a code that allows to immediately jump to the beginning of the next part. Write down that to resume the game in the future.

418291.overview: A PD/Freeware crosshairs shooter from Alan Petrik (Factor 6) and Petr Sindelar (Tuleby), released in 1995.

418292.overview: Serene III: The Final Battle is a single player, SEUCK based, top down, vertically scrolling space shooter by Fez Software released in 1992. It is the final game in a trilogy of Serene games including Serene: Next Raid and Serene II.

418294.overview: A one or two player SEUCK based, vertically scrolling shooter by Andrew Fez Fereday. It was inspired by SWIV, Z Out and Zenon II and released as public domain\freeware. It is the sequel to Serene: Next Raid and the precursor to Serene III: The Final Battle.

418303.overview: An exact clone of the game URIDIUM for the C64, this clone was created by Marcel Wolter, graphics by Arndt Rueger and Marcel Wolter and music Hans-Hermann Franck and released in 1992. Like Uridium it is a 2D, top down, horizontally scrolling shooter without bosses. Press F1 to drop bombs. 15 carrier spaceships have garrisoned your galaxy and each of these ships tries to steal a valuable metal. Destroy the defending forces of each ship and land on them, to accomplish the mission. On the spaceships there are several obstacles against which you quickly bang. Some aims, which you have to destroy, are positioned behind obstacles. Hence you have to fly back a few times to get at these aims. There are also canons which cannot be destroyed, but they send out drones which follow the player. Furthermore there are other things which can be destroyed. That's why the motto is: "shoot at anything which stands out from the background!"

418305.overview: A freeware overhead racing game for up to 4 racers made by Mike Dodd with music by Ste Bleasdale. The game comes with a level editor.

418313.overview: A sequel to the original Sky Flyer game, like the original this is a PD\Freeware game based on the SEUCK engine created by Andrew Fez Fereday. It features Aerial combat in a late WW1 setting where you need to take out enemy planes, ground emplacements and tanks all of which are trying to blast you out of the skies.

418318.overview: A single player PD\Freeware aerial shooter created using the SEUCK engine. It was created by FEZ Production and is the precursor to Sky Flyer II: The Battle Continues. Choose your plane, spend your flyer points, blast and bomb the baddies and upgrade your flying machine!

418346.overview: Game based on the Belgian comic franchise "The Smurfs" (aka "Les Schtroumpfs"), which was created in 1958 by cartoonist Peyo (Pierre Culliford). I consider Smurf Hunt to be a bit of a classic. Studio Peyo would not approve of a shooter in which you rampage through Smurf village, leaving bloody corpses and burning buildings behind. Pat Carson has blended Smurfs and S.E.U.C.K and come up with something fantastically memorable.  Game was included in a SMC (software of the month club) package.

418354.overview: Work on this game started in 1994 but was never finished by the author until 2017. A game similar to Project-X, a 2D horizontally scrolling shooter set around a futuristic alien invasion. Game concept, coding & graphics by Simon Jefferies. Music & sound FX by Joe Hanny.

418357.overview: A single-player, shareware crosshairs shooter created in AMOS by Robert W. Benjamin and released in 1998.

418358.overview: Coverdisk available on Amiga Fun #35. Also released on issue 2 of Amigo!. This is not an ordinary racing game: it requires you to build immense skill to make your way through all the obstacles. Every time you crash against an obstacle, you will lose a life. You have to steer a car to the exit of the level within a limited amount of time. There are multiple pathways and quite a lot of dead ends. You need to memorize the most efficient route and carefully drive without bumping into obstacles.

418381.overview: In the year 2051, deep space ships keep getting destroyed by alien creatures that can't be killed with conventional means. A brave group of volunteers is sent out in space suits and an assortment of experimental new weapons from the "space pack" project. It is up to you to find out which one of the seven weapons works the best against each of ten aliens. Fights play out differently depending on which alien you fight and which weapon you use.

418395.overview: A shareware Bubble Ghost clone. SUPER BUBBLE REMIX was included on the coverdisk CD of Amiga Format #123. A game featuring 32 colours graphics in a vertical overscan screen, more than 10 songs and jingles, 40 levels with varied puzzles and traps, bonus display features, high score table with saving option, 50/60Hz support and at the end you get a nice end game sequence.

418396.overview: A German language, single player, PD avoid it game created by Günter Meister. Navigate your mini-sub through the underground cave system.

418421.overview: A strategy solitaire card game published by the Italian magazine, Amiga Byte as a cover disk in 1992. This is 'regular' solitaire. On the main part, you build down alternating colors, moving cards or piles of cards among the columns. If you develop an empty column, it can only be filled with a King. The Aces go into the upper left corner, and then you build up in the same suit. When you click on the deck, the next 3 cards are shown, or the deck is turned over.

418425.overview: A shareware Snake\Worm game for one or two players.

418459.overview: A picture is broken down into 42 individual squares on the screen, which are then also scrambled. The player now has the honorable task of restoring the unadulterated original state of the little pictures with his mouse. Ahh, I know that, some people will now say to themselves, these sliding puzzles have always brought me to the brink of despair since my earliest childhood! Exactly right, as simple as the whole thing sounds, it is difficult in practice; In addition, you have to fight against a time limit when you're playing Sliding. The controls work perfectly, the sound is quite entertaining- and the pictures themselves? Well, one can say that the "United Graphic Artists" justifiably bear their proud name, because the graphics are really well done. Incidentally, the game is also excellently suited for several players who (one after the other) test their skills.

418465.overview: A surprisingly addictive remake of Konami's classic shmup "Scramble". Game written in 68K assembly language. Coding by John T. Kennedy. Graphics by Colin Turner (XJ600) and John T. Kennedy. Music by Darren Irvine. Released in several magazines including Amiga User Int'l (Vol. 5 No. 7) (AUI superdisk #2), July 1991,  Amiga Power #10 (coverdisk 10), Feb 1992, and also in Magazine Publisher 3: Amiga Action #67 (coverdisk 2), Feb 1995.

418557.overview:
Following an inheritance, you decide to get into the hotel business. You face the challenges that are placed on a manager in this economic sector.
Staffing, pricing, promotions and all the other "little chores" of a successful businessman are part of their job. In the end, after successful management, there is fame. You run a hotel with a global reputation. A Steigenberger Hotel, of course. A guest arrives. Is the service okay? The pool in the Ibrer hotel complex doesn't have to be paid for at first, later it's a must. Welcome. A well-stocked hotel is the key to success. An excellent kitchen and a pleasant ambience are born into a good hotel and allow for a better room price.

418570.overview: A one to five player turn-based strategy game, similar to Dune 2 with multiplayer support via modem or Serial cable. In the near future, the world is divided in 5 power nations that will fight until the conquest of all the world You could use the tactics, spying and diplomacy to made it. The rest of little powers will fall under your control. The peace will be the goal, the peace when you are the only one leader on the world

418586.overview: A game with at least a fellowship with Boulderdash, in that is takes plays in a multidirectional maze and is a collect-and avoid type game. This game by Enigma Software Developments was released in 1992 and is a precursor to Muzzy. This is the first release of this game, using the original title from the Spectrum version and featuring music by Andy Brown, who quit the team prior to the development of the enhanced follow-up, entitled MUZZY.

418649.overview: This add-on ends the Spear of destiny storyline as you continue through 21 new levels based on Hitler's new atomic research laboratory. Includes better sounds and graphics as well as new enemy sprites, and some minor adjustments like for instance the inclusion of crushed rats as indicators of secret doors, new prizes to get, etc.

418652.overview: An unlicensed port from the DOS expansion pack. continues the story of the Spear. Jump into the shoes of "B.J." Blazkowicz once again and go into 21 new Wolf levels with new, more detailed textures, as well as new bosses and enemies, such as machine-gun toting bats. Other additions include improved sounds and some minor gameplay adjustments, for instance the inclusion of crushed rats as indicators of secret doors, new prizes to get, etc.

418654.overview: An educational painting and drawing game for kids.

418656.overview:
It's World War II and you're B.J. Blazkowicz, the Allies' most durable agent. In the midst of the German Blitzkrieg, the Spear that pierced the side of
Christ is taken from Versailles by the Nazis and secured in the impregnable Castle Wolfenstein! According to legend, no man can be defeated when he has the Spear. Hitler believes himself to be invincible with the power of the Spear as his army of destruction sweeps across Europe.

418680.overview:
An Open source conversion of 1997 PC DOS Build engine game Shadow Warrior by BSzili aka Szilárd Biró that came out in 2021. The 2021 version supports up to 8 players via TCP/IP. It works over the internet too, which was pretty cool, but it's probably best played on LAN with a stable connection. Lo Wang has been working as a Shadow Warrior (a bodyguard and mercenary of sorts) for the powerful Zilla Corporation for years. But when he discovered the evil Zilla's plan to summon monsters from other dimensions and conquer the world, he left in disgust. Realizing that Lo Wang might jeopardize his plans, Zilla sends his assassins after him.

Shadow Warrior is a first-person shooter similar in style and gameplay to Duke Nukem 3D. The game set in a generic "Asialand", which looks like China and Japan conflated together. It features deliberately immature and politically incorrect humor, as well as a protagonist who delivers regular one-liners, commenting upon the situation at hand. Much of the humor is derived from over-the-top, stereotypical portrayals of Asian culture (e.g. scantily clad young women drawn in Japanese anime style).

The player has to complete several levels, fighting enemies and occasionally solving puzzles on the way. Though the game primarily focuses on exploration and combat, puzzle-solving plays a larger role than in most other contemporary shooters. There are also a few sequences that allow the player to drive vehicles, some of which have mounted weapons. Like Duke Nukem 3D, the game's environments are interactive, allowing the player to manipulate or destroy scenery and many objects, often revealing secret areas. On a technical side, the game introduces climbable ladders, true room-over-room situations, and voxels (instead of sprites) for weapons and inventory items.

Enemies include evil ninjas with various weapons, "coolies" which carry a crate of dynamite and blow themselves up when near the player character, female assassins with crossbows, and many more. To combat them, Lo Wang can use a variety of weapons and items. Weapons include: Lo Wang's fists, a katana, shuriken, a riot gun, an Uzi (two of which can be equipped and used at a time), a rocket launcher firing heat-seeking or nuclear missile, a grenade launcher, sticky bombs, a rail gun, and even some enemy body parts. Many of these weapons have a secondary firing mode. Lo Wang can also find and use gadgets such as caltrops to leave in the enemies' way, or gas bombs to choke foes who happen to be near it.

418888.overview: A flashy Minesweeper clone that requires a TCP/IP connection. Emulator users need to configure a fast CPU, some Fast RAM, Kickstart 2.0+ the and bdsocket.library emulation. The creator added a lot of elements to the standard Minesweeper experience: online leaderboards, a title screen with music, multiple scrolling ingame layers, explosion effects, and alarm sirens that go off when the bonus timer is about to run out.

418925.overview: This platform shooter created by dotmos and submitted to the Retro Platform Jam#6 is available for a number of retro computers and consoles. Updates since the game jam on itch.io have fixed and improved the game as well as added a number of new levels.

418927.overview: In this classic game of Skinvaders for the Commodore Amiga, the gameplay is identical to the original Arcade hit, in that you need to not only survive by using the buildings\shields as a defense, but you must also destroy the enemy waves as they move from side to side and slowly drop towards you. And that's all there is to say, as if you've heard and or played Space Invaders before, you know what to expect.

420602.overview:
A native port of Dark Forces based on The Force Engine. In it you are Kyle Katarn, a former Imperial officer turned mercenary, now hired by the Rebel Alliance. After having stolen the Death Star plans from a remote facility, he is tasked with investigating the sudden destruction of a hidden Rebel base. This leads him to face off against Imperial General Rom Mohc and the various iterations of his Dark Troopers - cybernetic soldiers with the armor and firepower to turn the tide of the war.

Dark Forces is a close prequel to the original Star Wars movie trilogy. The game marks LucasArts' first attempt to enter the first-person shooter market. Instead of licensing the DOOM engine, like many competitors, LucasArts created its own internal Jedi engine. The Jedi engine contains advanced features over similar tech, including the ability to look up and down, jump, crouch, and limited support (in the build used for Dark Forces) for rooms (sectors) over rooms. The 3D models also make occasional appearances inside the game, as turrets or Kyle's ship dropping him off or picking him up from each mission.

Most levels have a fairly complex, often maze-like structure, and include various switches that need to be activated to change the layout of the level. Jumping is integrated into the gameplay, as certain areas can only be accessed in that way. In addition to weapons, Kyle can use shields to protect himself from damage, a head lamp to illuminate dark areas, as well as specific items used to counter environmental hazards. The player character is given a certain amount of "lives" per level; he dies permanently once he runs out of all of them. Game progress can be saved only between missions.

The game features fourteen substantial levels as Kyle works to disarm the Dark Trooper project. Many levels reference characters or areas from the Star Wars movie trilogy, such as a visit with Jabba the Hutt, a trip to Coruscant, and a battle through the interior of a Star Destroyer. As opposed to most first-person shooters of the time period, every level has objectives for Kyle to complete, ranging from grabbing a clue and getting out alive, to planting charges around a facility to demolish it. Cutscenes appear between key missions to update the plot.

420913.overview:
In the early 90s, when playing shot'em up was fashionable, the (4)seasons team (newly formed) attempted to make prototypes of games of this genre.
Despite their efforts, the team decided to abandon the project, dedicate themselves to other genres.
In 2010, the team decided to recover a small prototype converting it in a small playable demo, adding scrolling text and a small retro-music!

420916.overview: A shareware AMOS game created by Cas Prince in 1993. A maze game. Kill your opponent before they kill you!

420918.overview: An overhead Grand Prix racing game, written in Amos and released originally as shareware in 1991.

420919.overview:
The game is called Super Pumpkin Bros. This is an almost playable early preview of a plateformer arcade game for Amiga1200 series. The present level is "infinite" as you can never finish it. It just made to let you estimate the gameplay. The aim of the level is to switch all the red modules to green and collect a predefined appropriate number of falling hearts. If you let a heart touch the  ground you will lose a life. If you let an zombie worker touch you, you will lose a life. If you let a bullettouch you, you will lose a life, If you play too
much videos game, you will lose your mind (cheasy!).

420922.overview:
A game preview\demo created by Stefan Krake and released as freeware in 1993. In a distant future...
On Quasidalla i, the entire economy is in danger of collapsing because some very rare chips are found on a circuit board of the central bank's central computer. SPACESHIP 3254, which was supposed to deliver the replacement chips from Gerrod Vt to Quasidalla II, disappeared in hyperspace on the way, but fortunately it reappeared near Quasidalla Ill after some time. Unfortunately, a lot of more or less unpleasant life and machine forms had settled in the ship in hyperspace and caused quite a chaos. 
 
You own Quasidalla II's only stellar recovery operation, and you're tasked with recovering the missing chips from the spaceship. Unfortunately, you couldn't pay the lease payments for your super-modern equipment, so all you had left were some outdated H-recovery robots. Try to survive the antics of gallant life and machine forms and save the chips. All the hope of the planet rests on you.

420923.overview:
Spod Blaster has been on my harddrive for along time, but I never got
round to finnishing it (and probably never will...) because I'm too busy
working on a Zelda/Secret of Mana likr RPG (If you are a good music 
composer and want to help then please contact me.), but I decided that I 
may as well release a version of it, so I quickly slapped up an options screen
and this is the result

420926.overview:
Welcome to "Super Trail", the professional fast action game of skill
(incl. comfortable level editor and many extra fields).

Principle of this game is to guide a rolling ball as fast as possible along a long trail, to avoid the holes or jump over them, and to get as many points as possible in the end (what else?).
Many extra fields with special effects can make this task easier or much more difficult.

420927.overview: Far, far off in the distant extremities of the universe lies a little planet much like our own. On this planet lived a happy family of tiny red squashy blobs. The Sploggys! They lived an idyllic world and soon it would be time for the great festival of dancing, singing and games. But the evil planet snatcher would use the festival for his own gain, by placing helium filled balloons to float the planet and all the merry folk off into the cold of deep space. The evil lord learned of what the Sploggy family had discovered and took the parents, leaving the sploglings behind. Can the little ones fix the problems, will the Sploggy adults intervene to stop what might appear to be mischief? A PD demo version and a full Shareware version of this game are available.

420928.overview: STRATOPLEX has 7 sequences in total, and 3 of which were inspired by the Disney movie TRON, but they only made 2D video game versions of TRON, in which people for the last dozen years have ALWAYS FAILED to surpass the 1982 original arcade game.  Then, about 15 yeasr later, in late 1996, a game worthy of being called the sequal to the MOVIE ITSELF was created by Pete W Storonskij! (oops, that was conceited :)

420930.overview: The game was initiated in the beginning of 1995. Since then it grew out to be the biggest game yet! The inspiration for this game came from a few very respectable games.

420931.overview:
SNOWFORT lets you build snowforts and throw snowballs to your heart's content.  You can be any of the characters in Snowfort: a Player, a snowman, or Death.  Each has it's own special characteristics to master.  Battle between 6 players to gain territory by rolling up large snowballs to either build impassible walls, or throw them at your friends.  Players can
move and fire in all 8 joystick directions.  Snowfort defines the highest levels of playability ever in any game.

420943.overview:
The inspiration behind it came from a little racing game by Armin Harich
I found on the Assassins CD-ROM. I have included it in this demo for the
curious ones among you.

420944.overview: Super Gridder is an Amidar clone that was published in Amiga Supergame #4 Magazine in 1990. A 64 oldie in an excellent Amiga implementation! Hectic coloring game.

420971.overview:
A true fast and furious Race against time in this
Texturemapped First Person Perspective RACER!!!

420976.overview: A shareware racing game that came as a demo that could be upgraded to the full version by Patrick Wikstrom, it was released in 1995.

420994.overview: Based on a reconstruction of the original Super ZZT code from Epic Megagames, this Amiga version of the classic ASCII text. Super ClassicZoo is a fork of ZZT by Adrian “asie” Siekierka based on ClassicZoo. Its goal is to improve the Super ZZT experience while sticking close to the original engine's feel and keeping full compatibility. It was later merged into ClassicZoo 4.30+. The game consists of several playable worlds. The gameplay is simple, with the player controlling a white on blue smiley face that can move and shoot in four directions and solve puzzles. Even at the time of its release, ZZT was a technologically simple game using text graphics and simple sounds, , but its limitations served to fuel creativity and an impressive amount of users went on to create their own ZZT worlds using various available ZZT editors.

421013.overview:
“Son of Zeus” is an Amiga game whose development was unfortunately never completed.

 Displaying sometimes disproportionate graphics, it is in line with the Sword of Sodan type hack'n slash though the player is only fighting one enemy at a time.  It should have found a publisher in Electronic Zoo in 1992, but history reserved a completely different fate for it.

421194.overview:
This summer d4rk 3lf and I started to work on my older project that uses stardust tunnel technic but with a bit diffrent approach..
However, that's not what we want to show you now.

421197.overview: Amiga platform game made with Backbone by Czeslaw Mnich in 2013.

421209.overview: Thought I'd try a small demo of Streets of Rage 1 using Amos Pro 2.0 and see how far I could get. It just has one enemy who never dies and I think a third of the level, but it's only a demo.

421250.overview: A freeware demo adventure game created in GRAC and AMOS by Iron Gate in 2021.

421259.overview: Backbone demo created while also using AMOS by Steffen Baier in 2017. It is a platform game. Mike heard of a fabled treasure, the long lost civilization of the Incas. So he made on the way to South America. Hardly was he there when the adventure began. When he found gold coins in the jungle, it was clear that he was on the right track. What awaits our hero in the jungle and what treasure and danger will he find there?

421284.overview: Backbone Demo from Reentier with sections composed in AMOS and released as freeware in 2018. It is like it's predecessor, a platformer but now there are the dead and the undead to deal with! There are 3 worlds to explore with 9 different stages, Playing time approximately 1 to 4 hours. Mike has the choice between 4 different weapons. There are over 10 different zombies.

421380.overview: A 3D isometric RPG designed by Edward Grabowski, was scheduled for release in late 1991, but the Amiga version (along with the Atari ST conversion) never materialized in full form. It was however released as a coverdisk on Amiga Action 27.

421448.overview: The Original Flappy Bird , was a Langnese advert game. In this case you keep the copter up and avoid the flying dangers, birds and fast moving storm clouds. Grab the treats to keep up your energy all while mashing the button to keep airborne.

421828.overview: Super Blobble 2 is the sequel to the first shareware puzzle game that came out a year earlier, iike the earlier game this one was also created by Alistair Griffin of Vector 7 and this one came out in 1996. Rescue your little buddies while avoiding falling through the floor!

421844.overview: Soccer Rivals is a football management game in the style of a board game where you play against 2 other players (human or computer) and try to take your team from Division 4 to Division 1 and win the title. There are 32 teams to choose from and you have the choice of five skill levels. The actual game has the whole board going round the edge of the screen. The board is made up of various amounts of eight icons which when landed on allow you to buy and sell players, train players, adjust utilities like capacity, surveillance cameras and youth team. Other icons have random choices which have bad or good effects of your finances and team. The last icon is a small arcade sequence where you press S to kick a ball at a moving target, hit the target and you win money. In the middle of the board is your team and you can adjust the formation and select the players. Once everyone has had one move and are happy with their team selections then you play a match, which just involves seeing the match results. Each player has another move round the board and onto the next match..

422032.overview:
Shoot incoming monsters with your serial mouse in the shareware title by Michael J. Wilson released in 1994. Per the author it is a completely sadistic and totally xenophobic blast-the-alien-blobs game. There were 2 versions, a scaled down PD version with a code to become the full shareware version. If you wanted the full sounds, end0game sequences and intros and source code you chose the shareware key. 
 
The first manned mission to Mars made an amazing discovery. We are no longer alone in the universe. Unfortunately we share it with a bunch of primeval simple, single celled protozoa less than a millimeter across, which is the most advanced form of life found in the warm craters of Olympus Mons, a very large and active volcano. They are invading the main server system and if allowed to grow there for 24 hours, they will multiply and take over the entire planet. You pulled the short straw and have to take them out.

422092.overview: Kamikaze Chess (also named Kamikaze Chess or Suicide Chess) is where your objective is to play either a friend or the computer and try to lose all your pieces before your opponent. Released in Amiga Plus cover disks and as one of the 50 Games collection as Suicide Chess.

422266.overview: A 2 player fighting game with some vocals released as shareware by Avante Software in 1994.

422278.overview: This homebrew text adventure game was an entry (the only entry) in XComp. It is a parody of the television series The X-Files. You are Agent Socks Molder, Paranormal Investigator, based at Rozwelle Police Station. Most of your days are spent investigating UFO sightings, alien abductions, children with telepathic powers, extra-terrestrial bacteria and the like. But today, your supervisor, Agent Dino Scaly, has a new assignment for you. There's been reports of a giant, man-eating chicken being sighted around town. He wants you to check it out.

422279.overview: The sheep in Australia have gone crazy! A breeding enhancers that scientists made have turned them all batty! Shoot them before they get you. An AMOS game created by Lee Hesselden and released as giftware, a type of shareware where you give a gift equal in value to the effort you believe went into the game and how much you valued it. Blast the ever speedier and sometimes smaller sheep before they get to your defensive line!

422280.overview: A game created by The Judge and Melf of the the Bastards in 1991. A one or two player Snake game where you eat the blue dots without touching the walls, lines yourself or your opponent. Eating the blue dots increases your score and also the length of your snake.

422281.overview: A shareware computer software house management game by Duncan Gunn from 1993. It was programmed in ASM 68k. Own your own Software company. Hire staff and design what type of game you want to put out into the market.

422284.overview: A single player, SEUCK based game that is a vertically scrolling space shooter. Blast Klingons, Romulans and meteors and other fierce aliens as you try to reach a warp that no man has gone to before. A game created by Stew Perks and released under the company name Dynamic Eye in 1991.

422287.overview: Take part in this freeware movie quiz featuring many questions, created by Steel in 1995. The better you do, the better the music is, do badly and dogs and cats will begin to howl.

422288.overview: A freeware AMOS racing game from Michele Berionne where you can wiggle that mouse/joystick to get your snail to the finish line!

422293.overview: A game much like Speedball a top down sports game set in the future.

422297.overview: A very addictive game. Collect your passenger and deliver them to their destination whilst avoiding obstacles! Piloting a Space Taxi, you must pick up passengers from "pads" and carry them to whatever other pads they wish to go. Space Taxi features screens with varying obstacles and challenges that must be navigated in order to collect your fare. Although Space Taxis sort of resemble standard cabs, they operate on a different principle - the longer you take to deliver a passenger, the less money you collect. In addition to watching the clock because of an incentive to collect money, players have to be aware of their fuel supply. Run out of fuel, and you will crash.

422299.overview: A single player shareware RPG created in Blitz BASIC and published by Alan Broz in November of 1991.

422300.overview: Platform shareware game in-which you collect items and kill various giant killer apples. The full game contains 50 levels and sex end of level nasties. Primarily a platformer, with snowball shooting as well.

422302.overview: This was an entry in the First Ever (And Maybe The Only) Interactive Fiction Mini-Competition. It was written by Graham Fyffe using the pseudonym of 'GLYPH'. A Happy Special Magic Production by Glyph (1998 Mini Competition) to you. Enjoy this game where you just might learn the meaning of life and help a few sorry sods in the process.

422307.overview: A SEUCK based shareware shooter for 1 created by A. Smith. You are a helicopter gunship taking on hostile ground and air targets to get as deep into the enemy fortifications as possible.

422309.overview: A maze/adventure game. Choose your character and the scenario and away you go! Game created by Demon aka Dylan Thomas using GFA BASIC and released as freeware in 1990.

422316.overview: Similar to Tron light-bikes, take part as a line and avoid the other player in a maze in this 2 player freeware game by Tom Bird made in AMOS.

422317.overview: A freeware Boulderdash style game by Kalus Kramer created in 1987. Not to be confused with the Soft Art game from 1992.

422318.overview: A side-scrolling shoot-em-up game created by Sa Majesté of Pisteurs in 1993 and released in the AMOS Project X Influence PD collection.

422321.overview:
This SEUCK Game is called, Slap’N’Tickle by Sensible Software (This Game was given away with the special version of SEUCK distributed with CU Amiga Magazine)

In this vertically scrolling shoot ’em up, You are a Red Space Ship, flying throughout the worlds, You have plenty of fire power to take down everything what moves

As with all Shooters, Shoot anything what moves, from Pulsating Orbs, to Round Spinning Objects, avoid the Gun Fire and Bullets, and Have a Blast!

422325.overview: An AMOS, freeware snake type game with a twist. Bombs appear and you have to avoid them!

422326.overview: A freeware AMOS game created by Mark Potter in 1992.  A game which has a message in its title. We need trees! Here you must stop the little men with axes from chopping down the trees.  You are in a  bulldozer  and stop them by driving over them or shooting them.  It's not as easy as it first appears as the axemen move faster than the bulldozer.

422327.overview: A single player, shareware point-and-click adventure game created by Asa Margetts in 1994. There's a reward out the summoner who roams the streets and haunts a sky scraper and murders people at random. Defeat him and not only could you save millions of lives, but you could also find a reward of about 500,000,000 pounds coming your way! You begin in the sky scraper he is known to roam it is also known that he's not human or if he is, has one weak spot where he/it can be stopped (maybe). Find him and finish him, the summoner is out there.

422329.overview: In the secret tombs you are locked up by this terrible tyrant: Abacus the Evil. But Zork the warrior will destroy him together with the black crystal. Now you are Zork. Freeware game by Y. Lariviere and R. Lariviere in 1992.

422333.overview: A freeware 2d overhead view role playing game created in 1994 by Matthew Downie. A role-playing game in which you play as a sorcerer's apprentice.

422339.overview: A one or two player shoot em up game made in SEUCK in 1995 by Mike And Sprinter.

422342.overview: Move your ball around to get keys and activate switches and solve puzzles in this maze game. The final version came with a level editor.

422343.overview: An AMOS based spaceship shooter and strategy, shareware game created by Equinoxe and published in 1993. A demo version without save function was also available of this strategy and action game. Your task is to clean all sectors of Sigen aliens. The full version also allowed second drive access and updates.

422357.overview: Before the evil witch set eyes on the kingdom the grass was green, there was life. But now there is little green. You must stop the witch before the kingdom is totally grey with life non-existent. An adventure game by Asa Margetts. Choose the barbarian with a broad sword or the witch with magic secrets!

422358.overview: A two player dog fighting game by Andrew Thomas. Created and released to PD in 1994. Two worlds are at war, the energy crisis has hit and all forms of energy are incredibly expensive. So save your cash if you want to survive!

422410.overview: A freeware AMOS platform shooter by Paul Young from 1994. Destroy the monsters and collect the falling pieces of fruit. Gives a shareware-like request for a donation for the full version, but it is unclear if a full version was ever created.

422413.overview: A freeware text adventure created by The Dordt College in 1992. What a wash out holiday! You are bored to death in this remote corner of Sweden. That's is, until you discover a corpse in the woods...

422415.overview: Your spaceship has crashed on a planet and you must find yourself an escape plan. An AMOS game from the prolific Asa Margetts, released to PD in 1995.

422429.overview: Originally published as Freeware this SEUCK based shooter game by Terry M. Johnston and first released in 1989 and then later picked up and sold commercially (WITHOUT permission) by Courbois Software.

422466.overview:
An AMOS based Soccer management game with cards for random events, like some strategy sports board games. 

The game was created by Frozen Ice Production  in 1993 and centered around the teams and statistics for the 1992-1993 FA Cup.

422470.overview: A single player action game where you need to jump to the top level through open holes in the platforms. You may need to wait until two partial opening converge to find a full opening.

422482.overview: Build to the skies!!! Drop your tower pieces to build up the size of the building. Time when to drop the next part to build as high as you can, try for perfect matches and strings of perfect matches. Don't be distracted as you pass balloons or the moon if you can last long enough. Keep calm as high winds whip the cable faster and faster and just keep building. Game created in AmiBlitz3 by Sami Vehmaa with the release to gold in 2022.

422745.overview: Amiga Space Flight Shooter, Star Fighter by GeoSync media 1999. This is a space shooter for the lower spec Amigas that cant run Freespace. A game in the style of WingCommander. There are plenty of missions which can be attempted as the good guys, the bad guys or a rogue trader, who is only in it to make money. There are some fairly impressive cutscenes and an impressive music score. 100 years in the future and mankind is on the brink of destruction. You can make a difference!

422866.overview: An AMOS based action puzzle based on Boulderdash by Galaxya Software released in 1998. You get a free life after 10000 points. For some reason the third is the easiest in the set of puzzles.

422874.overview: A single player, freeware Star Trek Next Generation quiz in the form of a Startfleet Academy Examination, so you had better hit the holodeck and do some studying!

422875.overview: A German language shareware space strategy game much like Spaceward Ho! and Masters of Orion. It features 6 players who can use 2 serially connected computers. Game language is selectable, but docs are in German only. The game was originally a shareware release, but the final version was given as a "last gift" to the Amiga-Community.

422876.overview: A two player AMOS based freeware pong style game. Federation vs Romulan with some special balls that paralyze change speed or let you use weapons on your opponent.

422878.overview: Star Trek the Next Generation shareware strategy game from Terry Mc Intosh, released in 1989. The full shareware version was multiplayer.

422898.overview: A shareware game based on the Modula 2 engine created by Jimbo Barber and published in 1989. A strategy and space simulation game for one player on a 5 year mission in deep space, fighting Romulans and going where no one has gone before.

422902.overview: A single player freeware puzzle game created by Datalink in 1990. Recreate the picture by sliding the puzzle pieces around like a 15 puzzle.

423012.overview: Star Wars: Escape From Mos Eisley is a homebrew 2015 simple text adventure game created using AMOS.

423014.overview: A one to four player strategy game made by Bill Turchak, Lloyd Lowe and Randy Young in 1991. You can choose how long the game is by determining the number of turns between 0 and 999, choosing 0 will randomize the amount of time. Each user can enter a secret code so that everyone can leave and there is no way for them to play your turns in this turn based strategy.  Each player takes turns colonizing and developing a game map of many planets. Each planet has an industrial capacity, and these can be used to construct more vessels. The player can send ships to nearby planets to conquer them. The player can scan nearby planets, and can evacuate planets in an emergency. The player with the largest empire at the end of the game is the winner.

423170.overview: A single player puzzle game from Mental Image. Bonus levels have memory games. Featured on Amiga Power 15, disk 2.

423178.overview: This computer coloring book is another part in the Electric Crayon series and it has 30 pictures of different opposites such as Above/Below, Enter/Exit, Short/Long, etc., with famous characters from Sesame Street to color. Pictures could be colored from a palette of 16 colors. A mix button would "mix" the current color with the 15 other colors and give a total of 256 colors. Choosing a color and clicking in the picture do a color fill in the area clicked. The finished, or in progress, coloring was automatically saved to disk. Player may also remove all colors applied previously to start coloring from the very beginning. Pictures could be printed with or without a monthly calendar, description, or message.

423185.overview: An AMOS based shareware game by Data Soft in 1993, with a PD version and the full shareware versions available with the PD version only allowing you to play the first 5 seasons. Train your squad, review the tables, spy on your competition for an advantage, tweak your pay and your players and get the play by play on the game based on your preparation and statistics.

423207.overview: Schoolboy Sixes hands you the whistle and the clipboard and puts you in the position of the coach of a team for Six on Six football\soccer. Review the match info, determine the best match ups of your players vs theirs and determine what tactics will win you the cup when Sunday morning comes. An F1 Licenseware published game by Mc Cloud in 1998.

423209.overview: Shapes and Colours Under 5's:Shapes and colours is a collection of six programs designed to help children develop colour and shape recognition, an awareness of size, and the concept of grouping objects in to sets. This is the foundation for learning letters and numbers. Shapes and colours is totally mouse controlled making it easy to use by anybody.

423210.overview: Some shareware space shooter from Samsof Software circa 1996.

423211.overview: A freeware text adventure from JIP Soft in 1994. You start out your morning in the usual way and end up in the bathroom when you realize that someone is threatening your life and you need to escape and save your skin. Use the tools at hand, and your natural humor to get out alive!

423212.overview:
An AMOS based crosshairs shooter. You have 100 bullets and only head shots count. The game, made by Rupert and John in 1992 was tied by the media to the Dunblane massacre that came four years later. Penguin Public Domain was interrogated by the media over publishing the game in England. Schoolyard Slaughter is a simple game (albeit an offensive one) wherein players earn points for shooting school children in the head for sport.

The gameplay echoes that of the standard point-and-click shooters that were commonly being produced at the time, and features crudely drawn children darting across a fixed backdrop at varying speeds. One hundred points are awarded for each successful headshot, along with a brief animation of the unfortunate victim collapsing in a pool of his or her blood. The player receives extra ammo for every thousand points, and the game ends when the player runs out of bullets. After the game, players can qualify to enter their name into the "Sportsman Journal" (a high score list) if their body count is impressive enough.

423213.overview: A freeware space shooter for Commodore Amiga computers. Created with AMOS. Source code included from Scum Amiga Software in 1996. Hint: You get lots of points by getting destroyed. But survive some times to collect new lives to be able to lose more of them.

423214.overview: A driving simulator done in the manner of many flight simulators with a focus on the Ibiza SXi vehicle.

423228.overview: A freeware AMOS game from Amiten (Johnny Acedvedo and Phornee de goblins doing music) for the Amiga 500. Fire torpedoes at underwater threats and missiles at surface threats and be king of the seas.

423240.overview: A SEUCK based shooter for one or two players by Brazzle Atkins in 1990. The streets of East London are an oasis of crime - and it is your job to clean them up! Using your trusty scum-mobile you must blast or ram everythings that moves. But watch out as some will bite back. Collect the baggies and clear up the blood for bonus points. Waring: some bags can send you sky-high!! Choose from three levels of difficulty.

423244.overview: An AMOS based horror\Halloween themed text adventure game from Bjergelandevej Software Productions and released as freeware in 1993.

423272.overview: A homebrew SEUCK based game by Bob Van Allen, released as freeware in 1990. You take off from the USS Midway in your P-38 Lightning and must blast the Zeros and other enemy planes as well as destroy subs and another enemy ships and ground installations. Grab the balloons for upgrades as you fight to survive.

423273.overview: A shareware helicopter shooter from James Hall. Blast the enemy aircraft, avoid the bombs and keep your energy level up or all will be lost.

423274.overview: A game where you pick from random cards to determine the results of your league soccer games. Pull good cards and come out on top, believe in the heart of the cards!

423277.overview: Eat all the dots but not your own tail! A snake\worm shareware game from Roger Schuttelaar and released in 1988.

423278.overview: Snowy is a game for kids featuring 2 sub games, Pairs and Snakes and Ladders. Walk through Snowtown and pick the place for the fun you want. Or maybe you want to go to the party down the lane. A freeware game by John Knight in 1992.

423280.overview:
Got fourth place in the Retro Komp Gamedev Compo 2016. Simulates a drag racing, where two cars compete. The game was developed on an A500 with one Megabyte RAM. During the game, the player is tasked with accelerating as quickly as possible. A car with low coefficients will be more sensitive to steering slip, which will make trajectory correction necessary. The absence of trajectory correction causes the car to rub against the protective elements of the track. Collisions with track elements cause the car to slow down, and it's up to the player to avoid them. You will need to accelerate to avoid overheating the engine. The aim of the game is to eventually win more races and thus earn money to upgrade the current car or buy new vehicles.

The player will have the option to set a stake/bet to win or lose a race. The winnings will be added to the overall score and will constitute the game currency. The budget can be spent on improving the car by upgrading several coefficients that improve the characteristics of our racer.

The game screen is divided into 3 sections. The first from the top is the part where the main race takes place. Below are markers for the car's current position relative to the total length of the track. Below, in the lower part of the screen, indicators for the first player from the left: speedometer, tachometer, engine temperature, current gear number and status of the “Nitro” turbo boost. In the lower right corner are the second player's indicators, positioned and similar in layout and function to the first player's potentiometers.

423281.overview: An unfinished attempt at a fully-fledged Wipeout clone for the Amiga using some new techniques to get some really fast texture mapping without cutting corners on visual effects. The game was created by Niki Hemmings in 1996.

423284.overview: Ski Master is as simple to master and play as was the original Intellivision game it was modeled after with the full fun-factor of the original game intact. It has two different courses to try: Rescue the Avalanche Survivors and Get the Flags as well as your basic Downhill Skiing game. It has 3 difficulties of play to spice things up. It also contains graphics certainly better than the original, digitized speech and sound effects. Created by Robert W. Benjamin and released as freeware in 1997.

423286.overview: A Red vs. Blue dueling game featuring World War I bi-planes and featured in the October 1990 Commodore User Collection 6 coverdisk.

423292.overview: A single player German language soccer\football management game focused on the 1988 season and released that same year by Steffan Schwarz as freeware.

423298.overview: A simple space shooter with some great attention to detail created using the SEUCK game engine. It was created by Russell Smith and released as freeware in 1997.  In general shoot everything, but pick up the heart cards\canisters when you see them. Two player coop is available, each of the ships is distinct in firing range and speed.

423299.overview: A single player homebrew AMOS shooter created by Timo Kloss in 2002.

423301.overview: An AMOS homebrew space duel style game for one player, created by Timo Kloss in 1994. The game came with source code included.

423303.overview:
Vertical space shooter game for Commodore Amiga computers. Created with AMOS. Source code included.
Hints: Press “e” to exit shop screen. Press “b” to use beam.

423304.overview: An action duel created as a playable demo by Amigos Development in 1993.  Fly your ship around and smash the ball with it to move the ball towards and hopefully into your friend\foe's goal it before they do the same to you! Like Air Hockey except you fly the paddle!

423305.overview: A five reel video poker\poker style slot machine game created as shareware by Alpha Software in 1991.

423309.overview: A Swedish language freeware text adventure game where you are given multiple choices and must pick the best option to move on. It was created by the Sug Ror Association in 1995. It appears to be a farce, and a lot of fun. Be careful, or you may be eaten by a grue....or a lion.

423314.overview: An AMOS based point and click educational game created by David Alexander and released as freeware in 1991. Drawing games, a doll house, football, story book time, use these and other tools to make your way in the magic lands.

423315.overview: A Swedish language text adventure written by Massive in 1993 and released as freeware. This is the real continuation of the quirky Jörgen i Köket. Unfortunately, there is a different game called Knapp Jörgen 2 - The Return, already so hopefully no confusion. And that other game what we'd like to call an incredibly poor attempt at imitation, but we won't! Torla the Power Man doesn't stoop to that level! Enjoy!

423316.overview: An unreleased Ping Pong game from Cool Productions in 1991. John Smith is an average player. Who wants to test his luck this year. To be able to take the trophy with you. he has to face difficult opponents! The preliminary round consists of eight games. The games are decided according to the knockout system, followed by the main round with the remaining seven games. The first player to reach 7 points wins, the game is over and you get an additional 500 points.

423318.overview: A space shoot-em-up made with the SEUCK by Dominic Beadle and published by Courbois Software in 1991.

423320.overview: A German language text adventure created by Samuel Verschelde. The S16 space station, in orbit around Saturn, no longer gives any sign of life. With the help of your teammate Nadia by radio, you have a mission to find out why.

423321.overview: An AMOS based freeware flight simulator created by Nicky Igoe in 1996.

423322.overview: Spéléologie en Aveugle! or Blind Caving is a French language text adventure, cave exploration game used to text Z-machine\Inform to Moika and back to Zmachine\Inform by BatteMan in 2020.

423324.overview:
Brutal Speed was a racing game planned for the AGA Amiga, briefly previewed in Italian Games Machine magazine issue 65 under the name of Speed Mania. It was also known as Speed ManiaX and eventually evolved into Brutal Speed. It was an impressive title that had 8 directional scroll at 1/4 pixels and 128 colours in total. It was similar in many ways to Super Cars 2, Overdrive and the likes of Neo Drift on the Neo Geo.

Although progressing very well and looking brilliant, it was just too late and along with several other games, it was cancelled. Previously the team had released another game which hardly sold at all, and just got pirated and spread everywhere. They decided to move onto other platforms instead, where they still go today over at https://www.xteamsoftware.com/

Sadly the developer confirmed they had lost pretty much everything when their A4000 HD had broke down. They have suggested that there might be backups, so something in the future could be recovered perhaps.

A playable demo was however released many moons ago when the game was known as Speed ManiaX, so you can at least check that out and see the promise of the title for yourself. Hopefully in the future we will get to learn more about the project and perhaps even find something more of the final game at the point of its cancellation.

423325.overview: A shareware Star Wars trivia game, where the demo version was freely distributable and the full shareware version included questions about almost everything in the StarWars cannon. V1.06 includes 145 questions and there are more to come. The demo version only had 25. Features in v1.06 are greater stability, especially at shutdown, support to use mouse to answer the questions and more hardware and Kickstarts. May the Force be with you, always!

423327.overview: Ah the rivalry. Atari ST vs Commodore Amiga literally in this dueling shooter from Marskilla in 2018.

423328.overview: An educational F1 Licenseware game created by John Knight and released in 1995. the game has sections for those 3-6, 7-10 and 11 plus and offers word puzzles where you guess the word like hangman.

423329.overview: Street Fighter in Istanbul. a ROM hack by Bronx and Crash. Released 1993.

423332.overview:
SUB-SIM:
Coding - K. Breslin Graphics - M. Brady
You are about to play a 2 player demo of the sexiest 3 player game available for your amiga today, enjoy it and please pass it on to your friends. Once you have experienced the sheer fun of the two player demo you will realize that the full 3 player game is a must for your games collection. Here's how to get your hands on this amazing game: Send a fiver (or equivalent in your own currency) to us at the address below (including your own address) and mention that it is sub sim that you want and we will rush you a copy in the next post.

423333.overview: Almost a comic book type story written from the perspective of a high school student. Created by Nagasoft using AMOS and released as public domain in 1995.

423340.overview: A shareware shooter created by Kevin Kendall and released as part of the AMIGA CD Software 2000 Volume 1 SET 2 collection. Work your way through the five zones: Forest, City, Sea, The Beast and Clear piloting your flying attack craft and blasting the foes that come out to take you on. This game throws things at you from every direction.

423342.overview: Super Combat II is a freeware, two player Gauntlet style combat game from Hambo Productions in 1992.

423346.overview: A homebrew, single-player version of Pac-Man created by Wer-Soft in 1989. Gobble up the dots and avoid the baddies, clear off the dots from the level to move on to the next one.

423348.overview: A German language game created in AmigaBasic by Christian Rodemeyer in 1988. An incomparable game, well done but quite unlike games you will find elsewhere.

423458.overview: An AMOS based Licenceware release created by Transvamp in 1994. Like many of these were intended to be sold as a cottage industry to bars and churches and places that would put on Bingo games for a crowd in front of a computer display. This one even has the number caller as part of the program and will print out BINGO cards for the players.

423463.overview: Get on your skateboard and cause mayhem as Bart in this single player SEUCK game by Marc Hart, made in 1990.

423597.overview: In this Amiga take on the classic vector game, two ships are controlled by two players, flying around a sun, fighting gravity and trying to blow each other to bits. Options include variable gravity, a black hole, an extra orbiting moon, toroidal space, and playing across a modem connection.  This one features a battle between a Star Trek and a vaguely Star Wars ship, so be team Trek or team Empire!

423604.overview: Not to be confused with the popular laserdisc based game related to Dragon's Lair. this harkens back to an even earlier shooting game with a first person cockpit perspective. The player can scroll his view in eight directions and lock his current vector to keep moving in that direction. Space ships will appear scrolling through the game world which have to be shot down. Some space ships also try to fire back at the player. The game is over when the shields of the player are depleted.

423610.overview: Red Amiga Ball vs Blue Amiga Ball for two players in this game by Michael Stickler from 1988.

423670.overview: Schiaccia Muri otherwise known as Crazy Wall is a bat and ball game like Breakout or Arkanoid where you must maneuver the bat under the ball to keep the ball in play and knocking out the bricks above until you have cleared all of them on the screen to move to the next level of play. This game was made by System-A software and released as freeware in 1990.

423681.overview: A glorious freeware shooter created by James Cleverdon in 1994. Your ships are orbiting a star (or two as you can control all options). Navigate the gravity and blast your opponent before they blast you! Use gravity to direct shots. Has support for two button joysticks. Use shields for protection and hyperspace is available.

423687.overview: An AMOS based shareware game created and published by Edward Burcher in 1993. Choose how many points for the win, define the ranking system and the League Title name and the number of teams in the league. Multiple league data files to choose from, so you can pick your favorite players on your favorite years teams. Manage your teams from the first goal to the trophy ceremony.

423688.overview: An AMOS based freeware game that was never finished and still not fully functioning, created by Retro1234 in 2016.

423691.overview: Game story line by Chris Mair. Coding by Michael Krehan; game engine by John Hendrikx. Graphics by Zak Jarvis and Steve Bara. Level editing by Rowan Crawford. The released demo of SHADE utilises the TextDemo V5.7 game engine. This was an attempt to transfer a 2D map creation into a full Doom-like experience for the A1200 and above, but it never progressed into a full shooter experience.

423693.overview: A single player puzzle game where the object of the game is to move your piece from the bottom row to the top row while avoiding the arrows. Arrows will always move in the direction indicated. Arrows will also wrap around on the board. If an arrow is blocked by another arrow it will continue to move until an open square is found. Part of strategy of Stepz! is to guess the order in which the arrows move. Your piece is allowed to move in the four basic directions but can NOT wrap around on the board. A move toward an edge uses up one turn and this can some- times be used to your advantage.

423708.overview: The game Soumrak or in English, Dusk is another of the series of Czech text adventures for the Amiga computer from MKCS. The environment of the game is a little different from the previous ones.

423709.overview: Světák Bob or Worldly Bob is the story of a programmer who has to solve a series of problems on the way to the release of his game. the game is Czech language and icon driven and was released in 1993. Reportedly, SVěták BOB was the first officially distributed game that was commercially developed in the Czech Republic.

423712.overview: A version of the Sokoban puzzle game by Alderan S.C. in 1994. You work as a warehouseman; great fun for days, an attractive puzzle game, dozens of boards.

423725.overview: An insane Silkworm clone created by Resurrection Team and published by Bisoft in 1994. Strefa Ciemności (Dark Zone) is a typical shooter game. Hordes of alien ships are invading our Universe in order to take control over the Solar System and the resources hidden under the surface of its planets. A hero is chosen to defeat them with three ships (which do not differ much between themselves) at his disposal. Your aim is to guide your ship through the waves of attacking enemy ships. They are not shooting - they just navigate into your course in order to destroy you. You have to avoid them and, if you can, shoot them using a very weak laser beam attached to your ship (there is no way to upgrade your weapon). Sometimes, you may find a token that gives you a temporary shield.

423799.overview: A Polish language educational program focusing on supplying a creative space to learn math in the first three grades of primary school. SUPER BULI has a task of helping you learn math. The sets are prepared in four levels of difficulty. The questions include all mathematical activities taught in schools: addition, subtraction, multiplication, division and simple inequalities. The exercises take place in pleasant company, which makes it easier for children to perform activities such as the 3 primary tests. Tests usually resemble school tests. For good answers, points are added up at the end and converted into grades. A clock with passing time was added as a stressful difficulty. When moving to a higher level of learning difficulty, the range of topics increases. to the text problems tables to are given answers and instruction to fill things in. In the highest fourth the user is presented a desk with scattered teaching aids. There are exercise books for tests, a drawing pad with crayons for making your own drawings in your free time, and a CD player with five songs. It has mouse controls but they are somewhat unreliable.

423816.overview:
Sunny Shine on the Funny Side of Life is a promotional (still commercial) adventure which advertises L&M cigarettes. The player takes on the role of Sunny Shine whose car was destroyed by a steamroller. The goal of the game is to get the only existing duplicate car into Sunny's possession. The scenario takes place in Los Angeles.

The game uses a non-parser control system: the player moves a cursor on the screen and after clicking on an interactive object, a list of possible commands pops up. Puzzles are mostly inventory and conversations-based. Special puzzles are a quiz about American pop culture as a first puzzle and a few action sequences. However, there are various dead end scenarios (missing an item which is required in a later scene) and a limited inventory. To pick up a new item after the limit is reached, an object has to be permanently removed from the game. The advertising consists of references to L&M in the background graphics and dialogues.

423938.overview: Gotta. Go. Fast. While there was to be an Amiga port of the Sega Genesis platformer in 1992, that never materialized into a working game. This 2008 creation by Rebel is a fan-game project and includes the full Backbone package with all the necessary files to get you started making your own levels. If you want to help finish this project off, all the tools are available to you now! Like the original, The plot of the game is simple. The evil Dr. Robotnik has captured many of Sonic's animal friends and trapped them inside robots. Fortunately, Sonic can free his friends by destroying the robots with his spin attack. Grab coins and move fast, be a whole new speed of hero!

423984.overview: This is a derivative from Gothic Vania AGA from demo in Scorpion engine by Erik i have remake the graphics to seems a medieval Stickman game.

423993.overview: SunMaze on Aminet brought 3D FPS Look and Walk to Amiga in 1989. This is a 3D Maze FPS game by Werner Gunther where you can walk around in the different kind of mazes with the numeric keys on your Amiga keyboard. You walk forward with the 8 key and turn either left or right with 4 or 6.

424002.overview: This is a snake clone for AMIGA i have built from a demo in scorpion engine by Erik and compiled by Toolkitman.

424285.overview: An AMOS based soccer\football management solo game from Frey United Software in 1999. Development was headed by Adam "Frey" Barczyński and his usual cast of characters, they created a number of freeware soccer\football games for the Amiga, supporting English, German and Polish language play.

424451.overview: Super Bagman is an arcade platformer with the difficulty from Bagman to Super Bagman taking the challenge from hard to brutal. The player controls the name-giving Bagman through several mine shaft levels composed of five screens each, his goal is to pick up money bags and put them into a wheelbarrow at the surface of the mine. Obstacles are pursuing guards, ore carts, and elevators. The only means of defense is a pickaxe, which stuns a guard temporally. The same happens when the player manages to drop a money bag on top of a guard.

424453.overview: A cross between Scramble and R-Type games, lots of goodies and upgrades to grab, keep your fuel levels up by grabbing fuel cans avoid the cave walls as they mean instant death. Blast missiles and enemy ships. Game made by Sławomir Maguda and released as open source freeware in 2004.

424706.overview: The Spelling Train: The carts contain various exercises. The lightest ones are in the red carts. and the hardest ones in the blue wagon. Click on the cart you want to practice with. Click on the train driver to exit. A Swedish educational game published by SPAB in 1991.

424712.overview: A Swedish math training and tutoring game created by Abris Data and published by SPAB in 1989.

424718.overview: How well do you know your Swedish geography? So well you can do it IN the Swedish language?! Then THIS GAME IS FOR YOU! An educational game created by TechnoSoft and published by SPAB in 1991.

425267.overview: Realistic tactical horse racing management game from ESP Software in 1991. In Stable Masters the player takes the role of a horse trainer to raise and train a thoroughbred horse in preparation of horse derby races. The player must first purchase a horse (each of which performs differently in racing). Then the player must choose a jockey that can ride and work with the horse. Finally the player must pick a race course. The player's choices affect the outcome of the race. If the player's horse wins, then the player earns money needed to fund the hiring fees and stable expenses.

425495.overview:
In Santas Present Drop 1, you helped Santa drop the presents down chimneys as he flew over numerous rooftops. In Santas Present Drop 2, Santa was unhappy that presents were being delivered to the wrong people, so he installed the Gift-o-Matic 5000. However, whilst flying over the Alps, the contraption exploded scattering presents all over the mountains.
Luckly however, Santa had his skis with him.  Your job is to guide Santa to collect as many presents as possible within the time allowed.

425569.overview:
An unreleased Codemaster's title that was unknown for 30 years until brought to light by Ashely Hogg and polished up by Brian Hartley for the 2023 holiday season. 

Stuntman Seymour is a side-scrolling platform game. The protagonist, Seymour, as a stuntman must make his way through four movie sets with different themes.

There are numerous enemies on each level, and collision with an enemy or its projectile, or falling into water causes Seymour to lose a life (he has 5 of them). Seymour can defend himself by shooting bullets that travel forward, or tossing bombs that fly directly upwards and then fall (there's a limited amount of bombs, but more can be collected on the way.) The levels also have score-giving items to collect. At the end of each level, Seymour fights a giant boss that jumps around and tosses bombs.

425693.overview:
15 Exclusive levels from the friendly folks who made Spheroid at Arkanixlabs.com. Spheroid is a puzzle game in which you guide a metal sphere around a maze of tiles towards the exit tile, within a time limit and set number of moves.

The maze consists of various hazards and tile types, each having a different effect on the metal sphere. There are 50 levels to solve.

Spheroid will run on any OCS/ECS/AGA Amiga with at least 1Mb of RAM and AmigaOS versions 1.2 up to 3.2. It can be run directly from floppy disk or installed to hard disk. And this special holiday version is a special present to you!

425793.overview: Help Santa get his presents back by storming the castle and then running around collecting them.

425796.overview: An action platformer by the BitBeam Cannon team created with the help of the Scorpion Engine.

425798.overview: It's Christmas Eve. Santa has to deliver the gifts, but be careful, so you don't wake up the kids or pets!

442413.overview: A train line management simulation game from the stalwarts of the genre, Ashley Greenup. In it you control the heart of the incredibly complex and busy Stafford station. You must make the trains run on time and get the freight safely to the proper destinations.

444009.overview: Severed Heads is a text adventure with location-specific graphics. Someone is going around raping, murdering, and decapitating women, and the player needs to figure out what is going on and stop the murderer.

447070.overview: Scopa is a popular Italian card game.

447229.overview: An AMOS based freeware puzzle from Grzegorz Gajkowski of Grino Studio. It allows you to rearrange the puzzle into a scene of sexual debauchery of the best kind.

448141.overview: An AMOS mini-game written by Tony Kingsmill, with music by Luke Miller. You control the screaming turbo speed machine that is the Lada Deluxe Mk. 4. Control the complex add-ons like Radio, doors, lights (candles?), four wheels and a roof!! With speeds in excess of 7 mph uphill and maybe 33 mph downhill...if you got some good speed up before hitting the hill.
